In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Ta-Ha﴾. Abu 'Amr recited it with a fatha on the ta and a kasra on the ha. 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Humayd [[In the Isfahan copy: Jamil.]] al-Azdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Jahm al-Samari, from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', from 'Isa ibn al-Rabi', from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: A man recited ﴿Ta-Ha﴾ to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. 'Abd Allah said to him: "Ta-Ha." The man said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, was he not commanded to tread on his feet?" 'Abd Allah said: "Ta-Ha. This is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to me."

They differed over its interpretation. 'Abd Allah [[In the Isfahan copy: 'Ali.]] ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is an oath which Allah swore by, and it is one of the names of Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is like your saying "do!" Mujahid, al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Dahhak said: Its meaning is "O man." 'Ikrima said: It is like your saying "O man" in the language of Abyssinia, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). Qatada said: It is "O man" in Syriac. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O man" in Nabataean. Al-Suddi related from Abu Malik and 'Ikrima: Ta-Ha, they both said, means "O so-and-so." Al-Kalbi said: It is in the dialect of 'Akk, meaning "O man." Their poet said:

"Indeed, foolishness is Ta-Ha among your character traits... may Allah not bless the accursed people."

And another said:

"I called out 'Ta-Ha' in the battle, but he did not answer, so I feared, by your life, that he would be a fugitive." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 16/171. The wording is: "Indeed foolishness is Ta-Ha of your character. May Allah not bless the accursed people."]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Its meaning is: "Tread the earth with your feet," meaning in the night prayer (tahajjud). Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by his height (or tallness) and his guidance, and the object of the oath is His statement: ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched﴾.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ta-Ha means the purity of the Family of Muhammad (ﷺ), then: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. [[Nahj al-Iman of Ibn Jabr: p. 85.]] It was also said: The ta is the tree of Tuba and the ha is the Hawiya. The Arabs express a part of a thing by the whole, so it is as if He swore by Paradise and Hell.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The ta is the opening of His name Tahir (the Pure) and Tayyib (the Good), and the ha is the opening of His name Hadi (the Guide). It was also said:

"The ta is 'O one who longs for intercession for the community,' and the ha is 'O guide of creation to the religion.'"

It was also said: The ta is from purity (tahara), and the ha is from guidance (hidaya). It is as if He, Exalted, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): "O one purified from sins, and O one who guides to the Knower of the unseen." It was also said: The ta is the drums of the raiders, and the ha is their awe in the hearts of the disbelievers. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ [[Al 'Imran: 151.]], and He said: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾. It was also said: The ta is the joy of the people of Paradise, and the ha is the humiliation of the people of Hell in Hell. [[In the Isfahan copy: in Paradise.]] It was also said: The ta, in the reckoning of the abjad (al-jumal) system, is nine, and the ha is five, totalling fourteen, and its meaning is: "O full moon (al-badr)." ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched.﴾

Mujahid said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions used to tie ropes on their chests during the night prayer. [[In the Isfahan copy: then it was abrogated.]] This was abrogated by the obligation, and Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When revelation came down to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makka, he exerted himself greatly in worship, and his worship intensified, so he would pray the whole night. [[In the Isfahan copy: for a time, until this verse was revealed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to ease himself, so he would pray and sleep, and this verse abrogated (naskh, meaning the replacement of a ruling by a later one) the standing of the whole night.]] So after the revelation of this verse, he would sleep and pray.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Harawi informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa al-Humaydi, from Sufyan ibn Ziyad ibn 'Ulaqa, who said: I heard al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood (in prayer) until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah not forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?" He (ﷺ) said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?" [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/251.]]

Muqatil said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You are seeking to abandon our religion," because they saw his long worship and intense striving. "We see that you are not for Allah, and that you have been sent to us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I have been sent as a mercy to the worlds." They said: "Rather, you are wretched." So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Ta-Ha. We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched﴾. [[In the Isfahan copy: The origin of wretchedness (shaqa') in the language is obstinacy and fatigue.]] ﴿But as a reminder﴾ [[In the Isfahan copy: and a reminder.]] ﴿for those who fear﴾ [[Asbab nuzul al-ayat of al-Nisaburi: p. 205.]].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is advancement and postponement in it. Its meaning is: "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you except as a reminder for those who fear, and so that you would not be wretched." ﴿A revelation﴾ is a substitute for His statement ﴿a reminder﴾.

Abu al-Shami recited ﴿Tanzil﴾ with a nominative (raf') ending, meaning: "This is a revelation from the One who created the earth and the heavens, the high (al-'ula)," meaning the lofty and exalted. It is the plural of al-'ulya, like sughra and sughar, and kubra and kubar. ﴿The Most Merciful, established above the Throne. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil (al-thara).﴾ Meaning the dust beneath the earths, which is moist dust. The Arabs say: "A moist (nadiyy) span," "moist night," and "moist pasture."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The earth is on the back of the fish (al-nun), and the nun is on the sea, and the two ends of the nun, its head and its tail, meet beneath the Throne on a green rock. The greenness of the sky comes from it, and it is the rock which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an in the story of Luqman: ﴿It will be in a rock﴾. The rock is on the horn of a bull, and the bull is on the soil. ﴿And what is beneath the soil﴾ no one knows except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. That bull has its mouth open; when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes the seas one sea, it flows into the belly of that bull, and when it enters his belly, it dries up.

﴿And if you speak aloud﴾ with the word, ﴿then indeed He knows the secret and what is more hidden.﴾

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Hamid [[In the Isfahan copy: ibn Muhammad.]] informed us: Bishr ibn Musa informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih al-'Ijli: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak, from 'Ikrima [[In the Isfahan copy: And Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas.]], from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His statement ﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾: he said: "What is more hidden is the talk of your own soul to yourself."

Ibn 'Abbas said, and it was related to me by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, from Abu al-Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Talib, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man ibn Musayl, from Yahya ibn Abi Rawq, from his father, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what your soul will speak of, what you do not know that your soul will speak of.

'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what has not yet occurred but is going to occur. He said: "You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you will conceal tomorrow, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what you concealed today and what you will conceal tomorrow."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what the son of Adam conceals in himself, and what is more hidden is what is hidden from the son of Adam of what he is going to do before he knows it. Allah knows all of that: His knowledge of what has passed of it and what remains is one knowledge, and all creation before Him is in that like a single soul.

Mujahid said: The secret is the deed they conceal from people, and what is more hidden is the whisper (waswasa). Zayd ibn Aslam said: Its meaning is that He knows the secrets of the servants, and that His own secret is not known.

Al-Hasan said: The secret is what a man confides to another, and what is more hidden than that is what he conceals in his own self.

Then He declared His own oneness, saying: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him. To Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Hamid [[In the Isfahan copy: ibn Muhammad.]] informed us: Bishr ibn Musa informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih al-'Ijli: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak, from 'Ikrima [[In the Isfahan copy: And Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas.]], from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His statement ﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾: he said: "What is more hidden is the talk of your own soul to yourself."

Ibn 'Abbas said, and it was related to me by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, from Abu al-Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Talib, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man ibn Musayl, from Yahya ibn Abi Rawq, from his father, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what your soul will speak of, what you do not know that your soul will speak of.

'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what has not yet occurred but is going to occur. He said: "You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you will conceal tomorrow, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what you concealed today and what you will conceal tomorrow."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what the son of Adam conceals in himself, and what is more hidden is what is hidden from the son of Adam of what he is going to do before he knows it. Allah knows all of that: His knowledge of what has passed of it and what remains is one knowledge, and all creation before Him is in that like a single soul.

Mujahid said: The secret is the deed they conceal from people, and what is more hidden is the whisper (waswasa). Zayd ibn Aslam said: Its meaning is that He knows the secrets of the servants, and that His own secret is not known.

Al-Hasan said: The secret is what a man confides to another, and what is more hidden than that is what he conceals in his own self.

Then He declared His own oneness, saying: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him. To Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾

The total of its letters is five thousand, two hundred and forty-two; its words are three hundred and forty-one (one thousand, three hundred and forty-one in the Isfahan copy); and its verses are one hundred and thirty-five. [[In the Isfahan copy: it has one hundred and thirty-five verses, five thousand and forty-two letters, one thousand three hundred and forty-one words, and one hundred and thirty-two verses according to the Basran count, one hundred and thirty-four according to the Hijazi count, and one hundred and thirty-five according to the Kufan count.]]

Abu al-Hasan 'Abd al-Rahim [[In the Isfahan copy: 'Abd al-Rahman.]] ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-'Adl informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Razi reported to us, saying: Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sulayman al-Hadrami and Khashnam ibn Bishr ibn al-'Anbar said: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami related from Ibrahim ibn al-Muhajir, who said: 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Dhakwan told me, from a client of the tribe of al-Harqa, from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, recited Ta-Ha and Ya-Sin two thousand years before He created Adam. When the angels heard the Qur'an, they said: 'Blessed is the nation upon which this will be revealed! Blessed are the tongues that will speak this! Blessed are the hearts that will carry this!'" [[Sunan al-Darimi: 2/456.]]

Abu 'Amr al-Furati informed us, saying: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn 'Abd Allah al-Sarakhsi said, from Muhammad ibn al-Fadl, from Ibrahim ibn Yusuf, from al-Musayyab, from Ziyad [[In the Isfahan copy: Ziyad ibn al-Hasan that.]], from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The people of Paradise will recite from the Qur'an only Ya-Sin and Ta-Ha." [[Al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/288, with variation.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Ta-Ha﴾. Abu 'Amr recited it with a fatha on the ta and a kasra on the ha. The people of Madina and Syria recited it with a pronunciation between kasra and fatha for both. Al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited it with a kasra on both the ha and the ta. 'Asim and Ibn Kathir recited it with emphatic pronunciation (tafkhim) for both. All of these are valid dialects. [[In the Isfahan copy: eloquent and valid.]]

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Umar ibn Humayd [[In the Isfahan copy: Jamil.]] al-Azdi, from Muhammad ibn al-Jahm al-Samari, from Yahya ibn Ziyad al-Farra', from 'Isa ibn al-Rabi', from Zirr ibn Hubaysh, who said: A man recited ﴿Ta-Ha﴾ to 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud. 'Abd Allah said to him: "Ta-Ha." The man said to him: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, was he not commanded to tread on his feet?" 'Abd Allah said: "Ta-Ha. This is how the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to me."

They differed over its interpretation. 'Abd Allah [[In the Isfahan copy: 'Ali.]] ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: It is an oath which Allah swore by, and it is one of the names of Allah. Sa'id ibn Jubayr related from Ibn 'Abbas: It is like your saying "do!" Mujahid, al-Hasan, 'Ata' and al-Dahhak said: Its meaning is "O man." 'Ikrima said: It is like your saying "O man" in the language of Abyssinia, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ). Qatada said: It is "O man" in Syriac. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "O man" in Nabataean. Al-Suddi related from Abu Malik and 'Ikrima: Ta-Ha, they both said, means "O so-and-so." Al-Kalbi said: It is in the dialect of 'Akk, meaning "O man." Their poet said:

"Indeed, foolishness is Ta-Ha among your character traits... may Allah not bless the accursed people."

And another said:

"I called out 'Ta-Ha' in the battle, but he did not answer, so I feared, by your life, that he would be a fugitive." [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 16/171. The wording is: "Indeed foolishness is Ta-Ha of your character. May Allah not bless the accursed people."]]

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Its meaning is: "Tread the earth with your feet," meaning in the night prayer (tahajjud). Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Allah swore by his height (or tallness) and his guidance, and the object of the oath is His statement: ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched﴾.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Ta-Ha means the purity of the Family of Muhammad (ﷺ), then: ﴿Allah only wishes to remove from you the impurity, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification﴾. [[Nahj al-Iman of Ibn Jabr: p. 85.]] It was also said: The ta is the tree of Tuba and the ha is the Hawiya. The Arabs express a part of a thing by the whole, so it is as if He swore by Paradise and Hell.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The ta is the opening of His name Tahir (the Pure) and Tayyib (the Good), and the ha is the opening of His name Hadi (the Guide). It was also said:

"The ta is 'O one who longs for intercession for the community,' and the ha is 'O guide of creation to the religion.'"

It was also said: The ta is from purity (tahara), and the ha is from guidance (hidaya). It is as if He, Exalted, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): "O one purified from sins, and O one who guides to the Knower of the unseen." It was also said: The ta is the drums of the raiders, and the ha is their awe in the hearts of the disbelievers. Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿We shall cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved﴾ [[Al 'Imran: 151.]], and He said: ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾. It was also said: The ta is the joy of the people of Paradise, and the ha is the humiliation of the people of Hell in Hell. [[In the Isfahan copy: in Paradise.]] It was also said: The ta, in the reckoning of the abjad (al-jumal) system, is nine, and the ha is five, totalling fourteen, and its meaning is: "O full moon (al-badr)." ﴿We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched.﴾

Mujahid said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his companions used to tie ropes on their chests during the night prayer. [[In the Isfahan copy: then it was abrogated.]] This was abrogated by the obligation, and Allah, Exalted, revealed this verse.

Al-Kalbi said: When revelation came down to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Makka, he exerted himself greatly in worship, and his worship intensified, so he would pray the whole night. [[In the Isfahan copy: for a time, until this verse was revealed. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded him to ease himself, so he would pray and sleep, and this verse abrogated (naskh, meaning the replacement of a ruling by a later one) the standing of the whole night.]] So after the revelation of this verse, he would sleep and pray.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad al-Harawi informed us, from Bishr ibn Musa al-Humaydi, from Sufyan ibn Ziyad ibn 'Ulaqa, who said: I heard al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood (in prayer) until his feet swelled. It was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, has Allah not forgiven you what came before of your sin and what came after?" He (ﷺ) said: "Should I not be a grateful servant?" [[Musnad Ahmad: 4/251.]]

Muqatil said: Abu Jahl ibn Hisham and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You are seeking to abandon our religion," because they saw his long worship and intense striving. "We see that you are not for Allah, and that you have been sent to us." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Rather, I have been sent as a mercy to the worlds." They said: "Rather, you are wretched." So Allah, Exalted, revealed: ﴿Ta-Ha. We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched﴾. [[In the Isfahan copy: The origin of wretchedness (shaqa') in the language is obstinacy and fatigue.]] ﴿But as a reminder﴾ [[In the Isfahan copy: and a reminder.]] ﴿for those who fear﴾ [[Asbab nuzul al-ayat of al-Nisaburi: p. 205.]].

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: There is advancement and postponement in it. Its meaning is: "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you except as a reminder for those who fear, and so that you would not be wretched." ﴿A revelation﴾ is a substitute for His statement ﴿a reminder﴾.

Abu al-Shami recited ﴿Tanzil﴾ with a nominative (raf') ending, meaning: "This is a revelation from the One who created the earth and the heavens, the high (al-'ula)," meaning the lofty and exalted. It is the plural of al-'ulya, like sughra and sughar, and kubra and kubar. ﴿The Most Merciful, established above the Throne. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil (al-thara).﴾ Meaning the dust beneath the earths, which is moist dust. The Arabs say: "A moist (nadiyy) span," "moist night," and "moist pasture."

Ibn 'Abbas said: The earth is on the back of the fish (al-nun), and the nun is on the sea, and the two ends of the nun, its head and its tail, meet beneath the Throne on a green rock. The greenness of the sky comes from it, and it is the rock which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an in the story of Luqman: ﴿It will be in a rock﴾. The rock is on the horn of a bull, and the bull is on the soil. ﴿And what is beneath the soil﴾ no one knows except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. That bull has its mouth open; when Allah, Mighty and Majestic, makes the seas one sea, it flows into the belly of that bull, and when it enters his belly, it dries up.

﴿And if you speak aloud﴾ with the word, ﴿then indeed He knows the secret and what is more hidden.﴾

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us: Hamid [[In the Isfahan copy: ibn Muhammad.]] informed us: Bishr ibn Musa informed us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Salih al-'Ijli: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us from Simak, from 'Ikrima [[In the Isfahan copy: And Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us, from Abu al-Ahwas.]], from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His statement ﴿He knows the secret and what is more hidden﴾: he said: "What is more hidden is the talk of your own soul to yourself."

Ibn 'Abbas said, and it was related to me by 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid, from Abu al-Tahir Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Talib, from Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man ibn Musayl, from Yahya ibn Abi Rawq, from his father, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what your soul will speak of, what you do not know that your soul will speak of.

'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The secret is what you conceal in yourself, and what is more hidden than the secret is what has not yet occurred but is going to occur. He said: "You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you will conceal tomorrow, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows what you concealed today and what you will conceal tomorrow."

'Ali ibn Abi Talha related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The secret is what the son of Adam conceals in himself, and what is more hidden is what is hidden from the son of Adam of what he is going to do before he knows it. Allah knows all of that: His knowledge of what has passed of it and what remains is one knowledge, and all creation before Him is in that like a single soul.

Mujahid said: The secret is the deed they conceal from people, and what is more hidden is the whisper (waswasa). Zayd ibn Aslam said: Its meaning is that He knows the secrets of the servants, and that His own secret is not known.

Al-Hasan said: The secret is what a man confides to another, and what is more hidden than that is what he conceals in his own self.

Then He declared His own oneness, saying: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him. To Him belong the most beautiful names.﴾

And has the story of Moses reached you, Muhammad? (The scholars of meaning, *ahl al-ma'ani*, said this is an interrogative used for affirmation. Its sense is: "Has it not reached you?") Some of them said its meaning is "Indeed it has reached you," and said: he had not yet been told of it, and then He informed him. Al-Kalbi said: his story had not yet reached him.

﴿When he saw a fire.﴾ It was on a Friday night. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Moses asked Shu'ayb for permission to return to his mother, and he granted it. He set out with his family, and on the way his wife gave birth to a son, on a cold, snowy night. He had also lost the road. So Moses struck a flint to make fire, but the flint would not produce a spark. While he was busy with this, he saw a fire at a distance, on the left side of the road.

﴿He said to his family﴾, meaning his wife, ﴿"Wait, I have perceived a fire"﴾, meaning he had seen it. ﴿"Perhaps I will bring you a burning brand from it"﴾, meaning a flame of fire. The *qabas* (brand) is a piece of wood or reed that has been lit, or something similar. ﴿"Or I may find at the fire guidance"﴾, meaning someone who will show me the way.

﴿But when he came to it, he saw a green tree from its base to its top, as if it were a white fire that was blazing.﴾ He heard the glorification of the angels and saw a great light. He was frightened and amazed. Then tranquility was sent down upon him. ﴿Then he was called: "O Moses, indeed I am your Lord."﴾ The repetition of the pronoun is for emphasis, to confirm the indication, remove doubt and establish knowledge. A parallel to it is His saying to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And say: "Indeed I am the clear warner."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 89.]

﴿So take off your sandals.﴾ (The reason for his being commanded to remove his sandals is as follows.)

Abdullah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Ubaydi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Najdah told us, saying: al-Hammani told us, saying: Isa ibn Yunus told us, from Humayd ibn Abd Allah, from Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Anbasi, from Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), concerning His saying ﴿So take off your sandals﴾: "They were made of the skin of a dead donkey." [Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 3/138.]

In some reports: "untanned." [Al-Sunan al-Kubra: 3/255.] Al-Hasan said: What is the matter with removing sandals in prayer, when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed in his sandals? Moses (peace be upon him) was commanded to remove his sandals only because they were made of donkey skin. Abu al-Ahwas said: Abd Allah came to Abu Musa at his house, and the prayer was established. Abu Musa said to Abd Allah, "Go forward." He replied, "You go forward in your own house." So he went forward and took off his sandals. Abd Allah said to him: "Are you in the holy valley?"

Ikrimah and Mujahid said: He only told him to remove his sandals so that the soles of his feet would touch the good earth, and he would receive its blessing, because it was sanctified twice.

Some said: He was commanded to do this because going barefoot is a sign of humility, and the early generations did likewise when they circumambulated the House.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: It was said to him: "Walk on the earth barefoot, so that your heel may enter the blessing of the valley."

The people of allusion (*ahl al-ishara*, the Sufi interpreters) said: its meaning is: empty your heart of concern for family and children. They said: likewise, in dream interpretation, whoever sees himself wearing two sandals will marry.

﴿So he took them off and threw them behind the valley.﴾ ﴿"Indeed you are in the sacred valley, Tuwa."﴾ "Tuwa" is the name of the valley. Al-Dahhak said: it is round and deep, like a *tawa* (basin) in its roundness. It was also said: it means "You are folding up the valley" (*tatwi*). It was said: it is the night; one says, "I came to you at *tuwan* of the night." It was also said: the blessing was folded upon it (*tuwiya*). Ikrimah recited *Tiwa* with a kasra on the *ta'*, and both are dialectal forms. The people of Kufa and Syria recited *Tuwan* with tanwin, as a sign of its being masculine and of its certainty. The rest read it without tanwin. He said: because it is *ma'dul* (grammatically altered) from *tawin* or *matwiyy*. Since it is altered from its original form, it is treated as *masrūf* (declined) from its case endings, like *Umar*, *Zufar* and *Qutham*.

﴿And I have chosen you﴾, meaning I have selected you. Hamzah recited *wa-innā ikhtarnāka* ("and We have chosen you") with the plural, for magnification. ﴿So listen to what is revealed. Indeed, I am God; there is no deity except Me, so worship Me and do not worship other than Me, and establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾ Mujahid said: "Establish prayer so that you may remember Me in it." Muqatil said: If you neglect the prayer and then remember it, then establish it. This is supported by what:

Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Marzuq told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Amir told us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever forgets a prayer or sleeps through it, let him pray it when he remembers it, for God, glorified is He, says: ﴿And establish prayer for My remembrance.﴾" [Sunan al-Darimi: 1/280.]

It was also said: it is connected to the revelation, meaning ﴿so listen to what is revealed﴾, and [listen] to My remembrance.

﴿Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it﴾. Here *akādu* ("almost") is a *silah* (a redundant, connecting element), as in the words of the poet:

*Swift to the battle, his weapons upon him,*
*So that his opponent can hardly breathe.* [Lisan al-Arab: 3/384.]

meaning: he does not breathe from fear. The benefit of this concealment is to frighten and to awe. Ibn Abbas and most of the exegetes said: its meaning is "I almost conceal it from Myself." Likewise it is in the mushaf of Ubayy, and in the mushaf of Abd Allah: "I almost conceal it from Myself." How then could any created being know it?

In some recitations: "How then should I reveal it to you?" Qutrub said: If it is asked, how can God conceal from Himself when He created concealment? We reply: God addressed the Arabs in their own speech which they understand. Do you not see that a man rebukes his brother, saying to him: "You have spread my secret." He replies, excusing himself: "By God, I have kept your secret even from myself, so how could I have spread it?" The meaning for them is: he has concealed it completely. The poet said:

*Days when Hind pleases me, and I tell her*
*What I keep hidden within myself of my need and my secret.* [Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/85; the phrase there reads: "Days when Hind accompanies me."]

How, then, does he tell her what he keeps hidden from himself? So the meaning of the verse is in this sense.

al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited *ukhfīhā* with a fatha on the *alif*, meaning "I reveal it and bring it out." It is said: *khafaytu al-shay'* means I revealed it, and *akhfaytuhu* means I concealed it. Imru' al-Qays said:

*They brought them out from their spending, as if*
*They were rain-clouds gathered.* [Kitab al-'Ayn: 4/314.]

meaning: he brought them out.

﴿So that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives﴾, meaning for what it does, good or evil. ﴿So let not one who does not believe in it and follows his desire turn you away from it﴾, meaning from belief in the Hour, ﴿lest you perish﴾, meaning be destroyed.

﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?﴾ He said: ﴿It is my staff﴾. It had two prongs, and at its bottom was a spearhead. Its name was *nab'a* according to Muqatil. [In one copy of the Isfahan manuscript: Mujahid.] ﴿On which I lean﴾, when I walk, when I am weary, and at the moment of leaping and vaulting. ﴿And I beat down with it﴾, meaning I strike the trees with it, so their leaves fall off and my sheep eat them. Ikrimah recited *wa-ahušš* with a sin, meaning "and I drive my sheep with it," since the Arabs say *hass hass* (to drive animals). Al-Nadr ibn Shumayl said: I asked al-Khalil about Ikrimah's recitation, and he said: The Arabs interchange *shin* and *sin* in many words, as in *shammata al-'āṭis* and *sammatahu* (to bless one who sneezes), *shanna 'alayhi al-dir'* and *sanna* (he poured the armour over him), and *al-rawshan* and *al-rawsam* for sealing.

﴿And I have in it other uses﴾, meaning needs and benefits. Its singular is *ma'rabah* or *ma'rabah* (with a fatha or damma on the *ra'*). ﴿Other uses﴾ is said rather than *ukhar* because of the rhyme of the verses.

Ibn Abbas said: Moses (peace be upon him) would carry his provisions and his water-skin on it. It would walk with him and converse with him. He would strike the earth with it, and what he needed to eat for the day would come out. He would plant it, and water would come out; when he lifted it, the water disappeared. He would drive his sheep with it, and it would protect him from vermin by God's permission. When an enemy appeared to him, it would fight and defend him. When he wanted to draw water from a well, he would lower it, and it would lengthen to the depth of the well, and its two prongs would become like a bucket until he had drawn water. At night, two lights would appear on its prongs like two candles, lighting his way so he could be guided. When he desired a fruit from the trees, he would plant it in the ground, and it would produce branches of that tree, with leaves and fruit. These are its uses.

God, glorified is He, said: ﴿Throw it down, O Moses.﴾ ﴿So he threw it, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly.﴾ That is, going quickly on its belly.

Ibn Abbas said: It became a yellow snake with a mane like a horse's mane, and it kept swelling until it became a *tha'ban* (large serpent), the largest of snakes. For this reason, in one place He says ﴿as if it were a *jann*﴾, which is the smallest of snakes, and in another place *tha'ban*, which is the largest. So *jann* refers to the beginning of its state, and *tha'ban* reports its final state. It was also said: He meant that it had the size of a *tha'ban* and the speed of a *jann*. As for the snake in general, it combines smallness and largeness, male and female.

Farqad al-Sakhi said: The distance between its two sides was forty cubits. When fear and the natural recoil appeared in Moses, because of the marvel he saw, God, Exalted, said to him: ﴿Take hold of it and do not fear. We will return it to its former state﴾, meaning to its original form and shape, ﴿as a staff as it was.﴾ ﴿And draw your hand to your side﴾, meaning your armpit.

al-Kalbi said: below the armpit. Mujahid said: under your upper arm. Muqatil said: meaning with your wing, which is your upper arm. ﴿It will come out white, without harm﴾, meaning without leprosy or disease. ﴿As another sign﴾, besides the staff. He would bring his hand out from a woollen garment of his, white, and it had a radiance like the light of the sun that dazzles the sight. ﴿That We may show you some of Our greatest signs.﴾ The word should have been *al-kubrā* (the greatest) in its grammatical form, but it was said *al-kubrā* to match the rhyme of the verses. It was also said that there is an implied element here, meaning: ﴿That We may show you some of Our signs, the greatest sign.﴾ Its proof is the saying of Ibn Abbas: "The hand of Moses was his greatest sign."

And has the story of Moses reached you, Muhammad? (The scholars of meaning, *ahl al-ma'ani*, said this is an interrogative used for affirmation. Its sense is: "Has it not reached you?") Some of them said its meaning is "Indeed it has reached you," and said: he had not yet been told of it, and then He informed him. Al-Kalbi said: his story had not yet reached him.

﴿When he saw a fire.﴾ It was on a Friday night. Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Moses asked Shu'ayb for permission to return to his mother, and he granted it. He set out with his family, and on the way his wife gave birth to a son, on a cold, snowy night. He had also lost the road. So Moses struck a flint to make fire, but the flint would not produce a spark. While he was busy with this, he saw a fire at a distance, on the left side of the road.

﴿He said to his family﴾, meaning his wife, ﴿"Wait, I have perceived a fire"﴾, meaning he had seen it. ﴿"Perhaps I will bring you a burning brand from it"﴾, meaning a flame of fire. The *qabas* (brand) is a piece of wood or reed that has been lit, or something similar. ﴿"Or I may find at the fire guidance"﴾, meaning someone who will show me the way.

﴿But when he came to it, he saw a green tree from its base to its top, as if it were a white fire that was blazing.﴾ He heard the glorification of the angels and saw a great light. He was frightened and amazed. Then tranquility was sent down upon him. ﴿Then he was called: "O Moses, indeed I am your Lord."﴾ The repetition of the pronoun is for emphasis, to confirm the indication, remove doubt and establish knowledge. A parallel to it is His saying to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿And say: "Indeed I am the clear warner."﴾ [Al-Hijr: 89.]

*Days when Hind pleases me, and I tell her*

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 24–52:

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.﴾ He rebelled, exalted himself, grew arrogant and disbelieved. ﴿So call him to My worship,﴾ and know that I have ﴿hardened his heart﴾ [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "wartantu" (I have put him in peril), and likewise in the passage that follows.]. Moses said: How can You order me to go to him when You have hardened his heart? Then an angel from the keepers of the wind came to him and said: Go, for we are twelve keepers of the wind, and since God created us we have been in this (post), and we have not known [anything of it]. So proceed according to God's command. At that, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, that is, widen and soften my heart with faith and prophethood; ﴿and ease for me my task﴾, that is, make easy for me what You have commanded me of conveying the message to Pharaoh; ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, that is, open it. Ibn 'Abbas said: there was a speech impediment (ratta) in his tongue. This was because one day he was in Pharaoh's lap and struck him with a slap and seized his beard. Pharaoh said to his wife Asiya: "This is my enemy." Asiya said: "Be patient; he is a child who does not distinguish between things and does not discriminate." Then she brought two bowls: she placed burning coals in one and jewels in the other, and set them before Moses. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue. That is the ratta (speech impediment). ﴿So that they may understand my speech﴾, that is, so that they may comprehend my words. ﴿And appoint for me a minister﴾, an assistant and supporter, ﴿from my family﴾. Then he specified who it was, saying: ﴿Aaron, my brother; strengthen my back through him﴾, that is, support my back; ﴿and let him share my task﴾, meaning the prophethood and conveying the message; ﴿so that we may glorify You much and remember You much﴾, that is, pray to You; ﴿indeed You are ever Seeing of us.﴾

The reciters al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ishdud bihi azri﴾ with a fatha on the alif, and ﴿wa ushrikhu﴾ with a damma on the alif, as a conditional and response, relating Moses' statement that "I will do that." God, the Exalted, said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses.﴾ That is, you have been given what you desired and asked for, O Moses.

﴿And We had already bestowed a favour upon you another time﴾, before this, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what is inspired﴾, an inspiration of inspiration (ilham) like the inspiration to the bee, ﴿[saying]: Cast him into the chest, cast it into the river.﴾ Muqatil said: the believer from the family of Pharaoh who made the chest was named Kharbil. It was also said he was a Copt (?) who made it of papyrus [Variant in the text: "min bardi", of papyrus]. ﴿Cast him into the sea, and let the sea throw him onto the shore﴾, meaning the bank of the river (the Nile). The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

﴿And so that you might be raised under My eye﴾, that is, be nurtured and fed in view of Me. ﴿When your sister walked along﴾, her name being Maryam, seeking news of him, ﴿and said: Shall I show you someone who will nurse him and take charge of him?﴾ That is, who will suckle him and take him to herself. He would not accept any woman's breast, so when his sister said this to them, they said: Yes. She brought his mother, and he took her breast. That is God's statement: ﴿So We returned you to your mother﴾, that is, We sent you back to her, ﴿that her eye might be comforted by your meeting and your presence, and she would not grieve.﴾ In the Codex of Ubayy: "fa radadnaka ila ummik" (So We returned you to your mother). ﴿And you killed a soul.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he killed a disbelieving Copt. Al-Dahhak, Qatada and Muqatil said: We afflicted you with an affliction. Mujahid said: We purified you with purification.

﴿And you stayed for years﴾, that is, ten years, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾, which is the town of Shu'ayb, three stages from Egypt [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "eight stages"]. Wahb said: he stayed with Shu'ayb for twenty-eight years: ten years of which were the bride-price for his wife Safura, daughter of Shu'ayb, and eighteen years he stayed with him until children were born to him.

﴿Then you came at a predetermined time, O Moses.﴾ Muqatil said: at an appointed time. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: then you came at the measure that you had been decreed to come at.

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. Then speak to him with gentle speech.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not be harsh in your words, nor severe. At that, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, that is, widen and soften my heart with faith and prophethood; ﴿and ease for me my task﴾, that is, make easy for me what You have commanded me of conveying the message to Pharaoh; ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, that is, open it. Ibn 'Abbas said: there was a speech impediment (ratta) in his tongue. This was because one day he was in Pharaoh's lap and struck him with a slap and seized his beard. Pharaoh said to his wife Asiya: "This is my enemy." Asiya said: "Be patient; he is a child who does not distinguish between things and does not discriminate." Then she brought two bowls: she placed burning coals in one and jewels in the other, and set them before Moses. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue. That is the ratta (speech impediment). ﴿So that they may understand my speech﴾, that is, so that they may comprehend my words. ﴿And appoint for me a minister﴾, an assistant and supporter, ﴿from my family﴾. The reciters al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ishdud bihi azri﴾ with a fatha on the alif, and ﴿wa ushrikhu﴾ with a damma on the alif, as a conditional and response, relating Moses' statement that "I will do that." God, the Exalted, said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses.﴾ That is, you have been given what you desired and asked for, O Moses.

﴿And We had already bestowed a favour upon you another time﴾, before this, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what is inspired﴾, an inspiration of inspiration (ilham) like the inspiration to the bee, ﴿[saying]: Cast him into the chest, cast it into the river.﴾ Muqatil said: the believer from the family of Pharaoh who made the chest was named Kharbil. It was also said he was a Copt (?) who made it of papyrus [Variant in the text: "min bardi", of papyrus]. ﴿Cast him into the sea, and let the sea throw him onto the shore﴾, meaning the bank of the river (the Nile). The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

﴿And so that you might be raised under My eye﴾, that is, be nurtured and fed in view of Me. ﴿When your sister walked along﴾, her name being Maryam, seeking news of him, ﴿and said: Shall I show you someone who will nurse him and take charge of him?﴾ That is, who will suckle him and take him to herself. He would not accept any woman's breast, so when his sister said this to them, they said: Yes. She brought his mother, and he took her breast. That is God's statement: ﴿So We returned you to your mother﴾, that is, We sent you back to her, ﴿that her eye might be comforted by your meeting and your presence, and she would not grieve.﴾ In the Codex of Ubayy: "fa radadnaka ila ummik" (So We returned you to your mother). ﴿And you killed a soul.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he killed a disbelieving Copt. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: at that time he was twelve years old. ﴿Then We delivered you from distress﴾, that is, from the distress and anguish of the killing. ﴿And We tested you with a testing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: We examined you with a test. Al-Dahhak, Qatada and Muqatil said: We afflicted you with an affliction. Mujahid said: We purified you with purification.

﴿And you stayed for years﴾, that is, ten years, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾, which is the town of Shu'ayb, three stages from Egypt [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "eight stages"]. Wahb said: he stayed with Shu'ayb for twenty-eight years: ten years of which were the bride-price for his wife Safura, daughter of Shu'ayb, and eighteen years he stayed with him until children were born to him.

﴿Then you came at a predetermined time, O Moses.﴾ Muqatil said: at an appointed time. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: then you came at the measure that you had been decreed to come at.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan said: at the age of forty, which is the time at which revelation comes to the prophets. [Variant in the second copy, citing Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "then you came at the measure at which revelation comes to the prophets."] Al-Kalbi said: the speech coincided at the tree.

﴿And I chose you for Myself﴾, I selected you, chose you and singled you out for the message or prophethood. ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs﴾, the hand and the staff, ﴿and do not slacken in remembering Me﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: do not weaken. Al-Suddi said: do not fall short. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: do not be remiss. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: do not delay. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "wa la tahanna" (do not be weak).

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. Then speak to him with gentle speech.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not be harsh in your words, nor severe. Al-Suddi and 'Ikrima said: address him by a kunya, saying: "O Abu al-'Abbas." It was also said: "O Abu al-Walid." Muqatil said: by gentle speech is meant: ﴿Is there in you a desire to purify yourself, and that I guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him?﴾ The scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is to be gentle toward him in your speech, for he raised you and treated you well, and he has the right of fatherhood over you, so do not confront him with something hateful at the first encounter. It is said: he promised him, in return for accepting faith, youth that does not age and a kingdom that will not be taken from him except by death, and the pleasure of food, drink and marriage will remain with him until his death.

The exegetes said: Aaron was in Egypt at that time. God, Mighty and Majestic, ordered that he and Aaron should come, and He inspired Aaron, who was in Egypt, to go out to meet Moses. He met him at one stage's distance and informed him of what had been revealed to him. Moses said to him: God, glorified is He, has commanded me to go to Pharaoh, and I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to make you with me. His statement ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ means: he will submit.

If it is said: how does He say ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ when His knowledge had already preceded regarding Pharaoh that he would neither be reminded nor fear? Al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Hasan] ibn al-Fadl said: it is directed to someone other than Pharaoh, and its meaning is: so that one who is mindful may be mindful, or one who fears may fear, when he sees My kindness and gentleness toward one whom I created, provided for, made healthy and blessed, and then he claimed lordship beside Me.

Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Husayn] said: I composed phrases modeled on it, saying: "This is your gentleness toward one who opposes you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is sincere with you? This is your gentleness toward one who is hostile to you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is loyal to you? This is your gentleness toward one who reviles you; so what is your gentleness toward one who loves you? This is your gentleness toward one who says you have a rival; so what is your gentleness toward one who says you are One? This is your gentleness toward one who has gone astray; so what is your gentleness toward one who has been humbled? [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript adds: This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who seeks forgiveness?] This is your gentleness toward one who has committed sin; so what is your gentleness toward one who has confessed? This is your gentleness toward one who persisted; so what is your gentleness toward one who affirmed? This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who sought forgiveness?"

It was also said: he will overpower us. ﴿Or that he will transgress﴾, that is, become arrogant and disobey us.

Moses said: How can You order me to go to him when You have hardened his heart? Then an angel from the keepers of the wind came to him and said: Go, for we are twelve keepers of the wind, and since God created us we have been in this (post), and we have not known [anything of it]. So proceed according to God's command. At that, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, that is, widen and soften my heart with faith and prophethood; ﴿and ease for me my task﴾, that is, make easy for me what You have commanded me of conveying the message to Pharaoh; ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, that is, open it. Ibn 'Abbas said: there was a speech impediment (ratta) in his tongue. This was because one day he was in Pharaoh's lap and struck him with a slap and seized his beard. Pharaoh said to his wife Asiya: "This is my enemy." Asiya said: "Be patient; he is a child who does not distinguish between things and does not discriminate." Then she brought two bowls: she placed burning coals in one and jewels in the other, and set them before Moses. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue. That is the ratta (speech impediment). ﴿So that they may understand my speech﴾, that is, so that they may comprehend my words. ﴿And appoint for me a minister﴾, an assistant and supporter, ﴿from my family﴾. Then he specified who it was, saying: ﴿Aaron, my brother; strengthen my back through him﴾, that is, support my back; ﴿and let him share my task﴾, meaning the prophethood and conveying the message; ﴿so that we may glorify You much and remember You much﴾, that is, pray to You; ﴿indeed You are ever Seeing of us.﴾

The reciters al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ishdud bihi azri﴾ with a fatha on the alif, and ﴿wa ushrikhu﴾ with a damma on the alif, as a conditional and response, relating Moses' statement that "I will do that." God, the Exalted, said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses.﴾ That is, you have been given what you desired and asked for, O Moses.

﴿And We had already bestowed a favour upon you another time﴾, before this, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what is inspired﴾, an inspiration of inspiration (ilham) like the inspiration to the bee, ﴿[saying]: Cast him into the chest, cast it into the river.﴾ Muqatil said: the believer from the family of Pharaoh who made the chest was named Kharbil. It was also said he was a Copt (?) who made it of papyrus [Variant in the text: "min bardi", of papyrus]. ﴿Cast him into the sea, and let the sea throw him onto the shore﴾, meaning the bank of the river (the Nile). The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

﴿And so that you might be raised under My eye﴾, that is, be nurtured and fed in view of Me. ﴿When your sister walked along﴾, her name being Maryam, seeking news of him, ﴿and said: Shall I show you someone who will nurse him and take charge of him?﴾ That is, who will suckle him and take him to herself. He would not accept any woman's breast, so when his sister said this to them, they said: Yes. She brought his mother, and he took her breast. That is God's statement: ﴿So We returned you to your mother﴾, that is, We sent you back to her, ﴿that her eye might be comforted by your meeting and your presence, and she would not grieve.﴾ In the Codex of Ubayy: "fa radadnaka ila ummik" (So We returned you to your mother). ﴿And you killed a soul.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he killed a disbelieving Copt. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: at that time he was twelve years old. ﴿Then We delivered you from distress﴾, that is, from the distress and anguish of the killing. ﴿And We tested you with a testing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: We examined you with a test. Al-Dahhak, Qatada and Muqatil said: We afflicted you with an affliction. Mujahid said: We purified you with purification.

﴿And you stayed for years﴾, that is, ten years, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾, which is the town of Shu'ayb, three stages from Egypt [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "eight stages"]. Wahb said: he stayed with Shu'ayb for twenty-eight years: ten years of which were the bride-price for his wife Safura, daughter of Shu'ayb, and eighteen years he stayed with him until children were born to him.

﴿Then you came at a predetermined time, O Moses.﴾ Muqatil said: at an appointed time. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: then you came at the measure that you had been decreed to come at.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan said: at the age of forty, which is the time at which revelation comes to the prophets. [Variant in the second copy, citing Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "then you came at the measure at which revelation comes to the prophets."] Al-Kalbi said: the speech coincided at the tree.

﴿And I chose you for Myself﴾, I selected you, chose you and singled you out for the message or prophethood. ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs﴾, the hand and the staff, ﴿and do not slacken in remembering Me﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: do not weaken. Al-Suddi said: do not fall short. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: do not be remiss. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: do not delay. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "wa la tahanna" (do not be weak).

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. Then speak to him with gentle speech.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not be harsh in your words, nor severe. Al-Suddi and 'Ikrima said: address him by a kunya, saying: "O Abu al-'Abbas." It was also said: "O Abu al-Walid." Muqatil said: by gentle speech is meant: ﴿Is there in you a desire to purify yourself, and that I guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him?﴾ The scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is to be gentle toward him in your speech, for he raised you and treated you well, and he has the right of fatherhood over you, so do not confront him with something hateful at the first encounter. It is said: he promised him, in return for accepting faith, youth that does not age and a kingdom that will not be taken from him except by death, and the pleasure of food, drink and marriage will remain with him until his death.

The exegetes said: Aaron was in Egypt at that time. God, Mighty and Majestic, ordered that he and Aaron should come, and He inspired Aaron, who was in Egypt, to go out to meet Moses. He met him at one stage's distance and informed him of what had been revealed to him. Moses said to him: God, glorified is He, has commanded me to go to Pharaoh, and I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to make you with me. His statement ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ means: he will submit.

If it is said: how does He say ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ when His knowledge had already preceded regarding Pharaoh that he would neither be reminded nor fear? Al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Hasan] ibn al-Fadl said: it is directed to someone other than Pharaoh, and its meaning is: so that one who is mindful may be mindful, or one who fears may fear, when he sees My kindness and gentleness toward one whom I created, provided for, made healthy and blessed, and then he claimed lordship beside Me.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: "perhaps" here is from God and is obligatory. Pharaoh was indeed reminded when remembrance and fear did not benefit him, and that is God's statement when drowning overwhelmed him in the sea: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims.﴾ [Yunus 90.]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard my father say: I heard 'Ali [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "Muhammad ibn Habib says: I heard 'Ali"] ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi say, reciting this verse: "This is your gentleness toward one who says: I am the god; so what is your gentleness toward one who says: You are the god?"

Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Husayn] said: I composed phrases modeled on it, saying: "This is your gentleness toward one who opposes you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is sincere with you? This is your gentleness toward one who is hostile to you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is loyal to you? This is your gentleness toward one who reviles you; so what is your gentleness toward one who loves you? This is your gentleness toward one who says you have a rival; so what is your gentleness toward one who says you are One? This is your gentleness toward one who has gone astray; so what is your gentleness toward one who has been humbled? [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript adds: This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who seeks forgiveness?] This is your gentleness toward one who has committed sin; so what is your gentleness toward one who has confessed? This is your gentleness toward one who persisted; so what is your gentleness toward one who affirmed? This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who sought forgiveness?"

They both, meaning Moses and Aaron, said: ﴿Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he will hasten to kill and punish us. Al-Dahhak said: he will exceed the limit. It was also said: he will overpower us. ﴿Or that he will transgress﴾, that is, become arrogant and disobey us.

He said: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both﴾, by repelling [harm] from you, ﴿I hear and I see﴾, hearing your words and his speech, seeing his deed and your deed. ﴿So go to him and say: Indeed we are two messengers of your Lord; so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them.﴾ That is, do not exhaust them in labour. He was amazed at it. But he did not see the staff until after that, on the day of the festival.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿gave everything its creation﴾ means the hand for grasping, the foot for walking, the tongue for speech, the eye for sight, and the ear for hearing.

'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Zakariyya, from Isma'il ibn Abi Salih: ﴿gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾, he said: He guided it to its livelihood.

Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿gave everything its creation﴾ means its counterpart: for man, a wife; for the camel, a she-camel; for the stallion, a mare; for the donkey, a she-ass. ﴿Then guided﴾, that is, made known, taught and inspired how the male comes to the female in mating. [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: His statement "that is, made known" comes after "in the act of mating."] Nasir read ﴿khalaqahu﴾ with a fatha on the lam, as a verb.

Pharaoh said: ﴿Then what about the earlier generations?﴾ Pharaoh said this to Moses when Moses had said: ﴿Indeed I fear for you the like of the day of the confederates, the like of the custom of the people of Noah, 'Ad and Thamud, and those after them.﴾ Then Pharaoh said to him: ﴿Then what about the earlier generations that you mentioned?﴾ Moses said: ﴿Their knowledge is with my Lord in a Book﴾, meaning the Preserved Tablet. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 24–52:

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed.﴾ He rebelled, exalted himself, grew arrogant and disbelieved. ﴿So call him to My worship,﴾ and know that I have ﴿hardened his heart﴾ [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "wartantu" (I have put him in peril), and likewise in the passage that follows.]. Moses said: How can You order me to go to him when You have hardened his heart? Then an angel from the keepers of the wind came to him and said: Go, for we are twelve keepers of the wind, and since God created us we have been in this (post), and we have not known [anything of it]. So proceed according to God's command. At that, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, that is, widen and soften my heart with faith and prophethood; ﴿and ease for me my task﴾, that is, make easy for me what You have commanded me of conveying the message to Pharaoh; ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, that is, open it. Ibn 'Abbas said: there was a speech impediment (ratta) in his tongue. This was because one day he was in Pharaoh's lap and struck him with a slap and seized his beard. Pharaoh said to his wife Asiya: "This is my enemy." Asiya said: "Be patient; he is a child who does not distinguish between things and does not discriminate." Then she brought two bowls: she placed burning coals in one and jewels in the other, and set them before Moses. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue. That is the ratta (speech impediment). ﴿So that they may understand my speech﴾, that is, so that they may comprehend my words. ﴿And appoint for me a minister﴾, an assistant and supporter, ﴿from my family﴾. Then he specified who it was, saying: ﴿Aaron, my brother; strengthen my back through him﴾, that is, support my back; ﴿and let him share my task﴾, meaning the prophethood and conveying the message; ﴿so that we may glorify You much and remember You much﴾, that is, pray to You; ﴿indeed You are ever Seeing of us.﴾

The reciters al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq and Ibn 'Amir read ﴿ishdud bihi azri﴾ with a fatha on the alif, and ﴿wa ushrikhu﴾ with a damma on the alif, as a conditional and response, relating Moses' statement that "I will do that." God, the Exalted, said: ﴿You have been granted your request, O Moses.﴾ That is, you have been given what you desired and asked for, O Moses.

﴿And We had already bestowed a favour upon you another time﴾, before this, ﴿when We inspired your mother with what is inspired﴾, an inspiration of inspiration (ilham) like the inspiration to the bee, ﴿[saying]: Cast him into the chest, cast it into the river.﴾ Muqatil said: the believer from the family of Pharaoh who made the chest was named Kharbil. It was also said he was a Copt (?) who made it of papyrus [Variant in the text: "min bardi", of papyrus]. ﴿Cast him into the sea, and let the sea throw him onto the shore﴾, meaning the bank of the river (the Nile). The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

﴿And so that you might be raised under My eye﴾, that is, be nurtured and fed in view of Me. ﴿When your sister walked along﴾, her name being Maryam, seeking news of him, ﴿and said: Shall I show you someone who will nurse him and take charge of him?﴾ That is, who will suckle him and take him to herself. He would not accept any woman's breast, so when his sister said this to them, they said: Yes. She brought his mother, and he took her breast. That is God's statement: ﴿So We returned you to your mother﴾, that is, We sent you back to her, ﴿that her eye might be comforted by your meeting and your presence, and she would not grieve.﴾ In the Codex of Ubayy: "fa radadnaka ila ummik" (So We returned you to your mother). ﴿And you killed a soul.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he killed a disbelieving Copt. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: at that time he was twelve years old. ﴿Then We delivered you from distress﴾, that is, from the distress and anguish of the killing. ﴿And We tested you with a testing.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: We examined you with a test. Al-Dahhak, Qatada and Muqatil said: We afflicted you with an affliction. Mujahid said: We purified you with purification.

﴿And you stayed for years﴾, that is, ten years, ﴿among the people of Madyan﴾, which is the town of Shu'ayb, three stages from Egypt [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "eight stages"]. Wahb said: he stayed with Shu'ayb for twenty-eight years: ten years of which were the bride-price for his wife Safura, daughter of Shu'ayb, and eighteen years he stayed with him until children were born to him.

﴿Then you came at a predetermined time, O Moses.﴾ Muqatil said: at an appointed time. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: then you came at the measure that you had been decreed to come at.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Kaysan said: at the age of forty, which is the time at which revelation comes to the prophets. [Variant in the second copy, citing Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "then you came at the measure at which revelation comes to the prophets."] Al-Kalbi said: the speech coincided at the tree.

﴿And I chose you for Myself﴾, I selected you, chose you and singled you out for the message or prophethood. ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs﴾, the hand and the staff, ﴿and do not slacken in remembering Me﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: do not weaken. Al-Suddi said: do not fall short. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: do not be remiss. 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: do not delay. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "wa la tahanna" (do not be weak).

﴿Go to Pharaoh, for he has transgressed. Then speak to him with gentle speech.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not be harsh in your words, nor severe. Al-Suddi and 'Ikrima said: address him by a kunya, saying: "O Abu al-'Abbas." It was also said: "O Abu al-Walid." Muqatil said: by gentle speech is meant: ﴿Is there in you a desire to purify yourself, and that I guide you to your Lord so you would fear Him?﴾ The scholars of the meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: its meaning is to be gentle toward him in your speech, for he raised you and treated you well, and he has the right of fatherhood over you, so do not confront him with something hateful at the first encounter. It is said: he promised him, in return for accepting faith, youth that does not age and a kingdom that will not be taken from him except by death, and the pleasure of food, drink and marriage will remain with him until his death.

The exegetes said: Aaron was in Egypt at that time. God, Mighty and Majestic, ordered that he and Aaron should come, and He inspired Aaron, who was in Egypt, to go out to meet Moses. He met him at one stage's distance and informed him of what had been revealed to him. Moses said to him: God, glorified is He, has commanded me to go to Pharaoh, and I asked my Lord, Mighty and Majestic, to make you with me. His statement ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ means: he will submit.

If it is said: how does He say ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or will fear﴾ when His knowledge had already preceded regarding Pharaoh that he would neither be reminded nor fear? Al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Hasan] ibn al-Fadl said: it is directed to someone other than Pharaoh, and its meaning is: so that one who is mindful may be mindful, or one who fears may fear, when he sees My kindness and gentleness toward one whom I created, provided for, made healthy and blessed, and then he claimed lordship beside Me.

Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn 'Umar al-Warraq said: "perhaps" here is from God and is obligatory. Pharaoh was indeed reminded when remembrance and fear did not benefit him, and that is God's statement when drowning overwhelmed him in the sea: ﴿I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims.﴾ [Yunus 90.]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Habib say: I heard my father say: I heard 'Ali [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: "Muhammad ibn Habib says: I heard 'Ali"] ibn Muhammad al-Warraq say: I heard Yahya ibn Mu'adh al-Razi say, reciting this verse: "This is your gentleness toward one who says: I am the god; so what is your gentleness toward one who says: You are the god?"

Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript: al-Husayn] said: I composed phrases modeled on it, saying: "This is your gentleness toward one who opposes you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is sincere with you? This is your gentleness toward one who is hostile to you; so what is your gentleness toward one who is loyal to you? This is your gentleness toward one who reviles you; so what is your gentleness toward one who loves you? This is your gentleness toward one who says you have a rival; so what is your gentleness toward one who says you are One? This is your gentleness toward one who has gone astray; so what is your gentleness toward one who has been humbled? [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript adds: This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who seeks forgiveness?] This is your gentleness toward one who has committed sin; so what is your gentleness toward one who has confessed? This is your gentleness toward one who persisted; so what is your gentleness toward one who affirmed? This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who sought forgiveness?"

They both, meaning Moses and Aaron, said: ﴿Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: he will hasten to kill and punish us. Al-Dahhak said: he will exceed the limit. It was also said: he will overpower us. ﴿Or that he will transgress﴾, that is, become arrogant and disobey us.

He said: ﴿Do not fear; indeed I am with you both﴾, by repelling [harm] from you, ﴿I hear and I see﴾, hearing your words and his speech, seeing his deed and your deed. ﴿So go to him and say: Indeed we are two messengers of your Lord; so send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them.﴾ That is, do not exhaust them in labour. The Children of Israel were under the Pharaoh's family in severe torment: they killed their sons, enslaved their women, and burdened them with labour, bricks, clay and building cities beyond their capacity.

Moses said: ﴿We have come to you with a sign from your Lord.﴾ Pharaoh said: And what is it? He said: he put his hand into the opening of his garment and then brought it out, and behold, it was white, having a radiance like the radiance of the sun, overpowering the light of the sun. He was amazed at it. But he did not see the staff until after that, on the day of the festival.

﴿And peace is upon whoever follows the guidance﴾, meaning whoever submits. ﴿Indeed it has been revealed to us that the punishment is upon whoever denies [God's prophets] and turns away﴾, that is, turns away from faith. He said: ﴿Who then is your Lord, O Moses?﴾, meaning, O Moses and Aaron, but Moses alone was mentioned for the sake of the rhyme of the verses.

He said: ﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation﴾. Al-Husayn and Qatada said: He gave everything its suitability and guided it to what suits it. Mujahid said: He did not make man in the creation of animals, nor animals in the creation of man, but He created each thing and ﴿then guided it﴾ [variant reading] ﴿measuring it precisely.﴾ 'Ata' said: ﴿gave everything its creation﴾ means its form. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue. The wording is an imperative, but its meaning is a report, metaphorically: until the sea casts him onto the shore. ﴿An enemy of Mine and his enemy will take him,﴾ meaning Pharaoh. She made a chest, put cotton in it, placed Moses in it, sealed its top and its cracks with pitch, and then cast it into the Nile. A great river branched off from it into Pharaoh's palace. While he was sitting at the edge of the pool with his wife Asiya, suddenly a chest came toward them carried by the water. When he saw it, he ordered the boys and girls to bring it out; they brought it out and opened its top, and there was a child with the most beautiful face of people. When Pharaoh saw him he loved him so much that he could not restrain himself. That is God's statement: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: He loved him and made him beloved to His creation. 'Ata' al-'Awfi said: He placed upon him a radiance of beauty such that whoever saw him could hardly remain away from him. Qatada said: there was a charm in Moses' eyes; no one saw him without falling in love with him.

﴿And so that you might be raised under My eye﴾, that is, be nurtured and fed in view of Me. ﴿When your sister walked along﴾, her name being Maryam, seeking news of him, ﴿and said: Shall I show you someone who will nurse him and take charge of him?﴾ That is, who will suckle him and take him to herself. He would not accept any woman's breast, so when his sister said this to them, they said: Yes. She brought his mother, and he took her breast. That is God's statement: ﴿So We returned you to your mother﴾, that is, We sent you back to her, ﴿that her eye might be comforted by your meeting and your presence, and she would not grieve.﴾ In the Codex of Ubayy: "fa radadnaka ila ummik" (So We returned you to your mother). ﴿And you killed a soul.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he killed a disbelieving Copt. Al-Dahhak, Qatada and Muqatil said: We afflicted you with an affliction. Mujahid said: We purified you with purification.

In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "wa la tahanna" (do not be weak).

This is your gentleness toward one who has gone astray; so what is your gentleness toward one who has been humbled? [Variant in the Isfahan manuscript adds: This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who seeks forgiveness?] This is your gentleness toward one who has committed sin; so what is your gentleness toward one who has confessed? This is your gentleness toward one who persisted; so what is your gentleness toward one who affirmed? This is your gentleness toward one who was arrogant; so what is your gentleness toward one who sought forgiveness?"

Then an angel from the keepers of the wind came to him and said: Go, for we are twelve keepers of the wind, and since God created us we have been in this (post), and we have not known [anything of it]. So proceed according to God's command. At that, Moses said: ﴿My Lord, expand for me my breast﴾, that is, widen and soften my heart with faith and prophethood; ﴿and ease for me my task﴾, that is, make easy for me what You have commanded me of conveying the message to Pharaoh; ﴿and loosen a knot from my tongue﴾, that is, open it. Pharaoh said to his wife Asiya: "This is my enemy." Asiya said: "Be patient; he is a child who does not distinguish between things and does not discriminate." Then she brought two bowls: she placed burning coals in one and jewels in the other, and set them before Moses. Gabriel took Moses' hand and placed it on the fire until he lifted a live coal and put it on his tongue.
