When Pharaoh reached the shore, he found that Musa and the Children of Israel had crossed. He said to the Copts: "The sea has been bewitched, so cross." They said to him: "If you are a lord, then enter the sea as it did." Jibril came on a mare in heat [in the Isfahan manuscript: "wa-dhaq"], while Pharaoh was on a stallion, the male of horses. Jibril drove the mare into the water, and Pharaoh's stallion could not restrain itself; it plunged into the sea following her trail, and all the Copts entered after him. When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

Ka'b said: The Samiri recognised the horse of Jibril, so he took a handful of dust from its track and threw it into the calf when he made it. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "when they made it."]

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Eat of the good things that We have provided for you.﴾ This is the reading of the common recitation with the nun and the alif, in the plural of majesty. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa said to him: ﴿Go, for in your life you will say, "No touching"﴾, that is, as long as you live you shall say: do not mix with anyone, and no one mixes with you. ﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*

That is, *ahassna*.

﴿We will surely burn it﴾. The common recitation has a damma on the nun and a shadda on the ra', meaning: we will burn it with fire. Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaysin and Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited *lanahruqanhu* with a fatha on the nun and a damma on a light ra', meaning: we will grind it with files. It is said: *haraqahu* and *yahruquhu* when he filed it down, and from this the file is called *al-muhriq*. The evidence for this reading is the statement of al-Suddi: Musa took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it into the sea. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "We will slaughter it, then we will burn it."

﴿Then we will surely scatter it﴾, that is, we will winnow it, ﴿into the sea, with a scattering.﴾ It is said: *nasafa al-ta'am bi-l-minsaf*, when one winnows the grain with a winnowing fork, scattering it and blowing away its husks and dust.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 77–97:

And We revealed to Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾, meaning: set out with them at the beginning of the night from the land of Egypt.

﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾, dry, with no water or mud in it. ﴿You will not fear being overtaken﴾ by Pharaoh behind you, ﴿nor will you fear drowning﴾ in the sea ahead of you. Hamza recited ﴿la takhaf﴾ with a jussive (*jazm*) on the basis of prohibition (*nahy*), while the rest recited it with an alif on the basis of negation (*nafy*). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading because of the following ﴿wa la takhsha﴾ in the raised form (*raf'*). The evidence for Hamza's reading is the verse ﴿They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped﴾, where the sentence is resumed (*fa-istaana'a*). Al-Farra' said: "If Hamza intended the jussive with ﴿wa la takhsha﴾, it would be correct." A poet said:

*"You satirized a time, then you turned back, making excuses,*
*for one who abused a time that neither satirized nor harmed."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/228.]]

Another said:

*"Has there not come to you, while the news spreads,*
*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/492.]]

This is the answer to Pharaoh's words: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. So God contradicted him, saying: ﴿Rather, He led them astray and did not guide them.﴾

So they became lattices, so that some could see one another and some could hear one another's speech.

When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*

﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his armies, and the sea covered them with what covered them.﴾ That is, the waters struck them. ﴿Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.﴾ That is, he did not guide them to their right course. Wahb said: The Children of Israel borrowed much jewelry from the Copts, then Musa set out with them at the beginning of the night. They numbered seventy thousand. Pharaoh was informed of this, so he rode out with six hundred thousand men from the Copts, tracing the trail of Musa. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "tracing their trail."] When the people of Musa saw the dust of the horses, they said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾. Musa said: ﴿No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾. When they drew near, they said: "O Musa, where shall we go? The sea is before us and Pharaoh is behind us." Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it split, becoming twelve dry paths, one for each tribe. Between every two paths was something like a great mountain of water. They passed through it, and they were all cousins, so that each tribe could not see the others. They grew lonely and afraid. God, glorified be He, revealed to the mountains of water: "Interlace!" So they became lattices, so that some could see one another and some could hear one another's speech.

When Pharaoh reached the shore, he found that Musa and the Children of Israel had crossed. He said to the Copts: "The sea has been bewitched, so cross." They said to him: "If you are a lord, then enter the sea as it did." Jibril came on a mare in heat [in the Isfahan manuscript: "wa-dhaq"], while Pharaoh was on a stallion, the male of horses. Jibril drove the mare into the water, and Pharaoh's stallion could not restrain itself; it plunged into the sea following her trail, and all the Copts entered after him. When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

Ka'b said: The Samiri recognised the horse of Jibril, so he took a handful of dust from its track and threw it into the calf when he made it. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "when they made it."]

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Qatada said: the Samiri was a great man among the Children of Israel, from a tribe called Samira, but the enemy of God became a hypocrite after the crossing of the sea with the Children of Israel. Then the Samiri said in answer to Musa: ﴿I saw what they did not see﴾, meaning I saw what they had not seen, recognised what they had not recognised, and perceived what they had not perceived. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited *tabsuru* with a ta' as an address; the rest recited it with a ya' as a report. ﴿So I took a handful from the track of the Messenger﴾, that is, I took dust from the track of Jibril's horse. Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa said to him: ﴿Go, for in your life you will say, "No touching"﴾, that is, as long as you live you shall say: do not mix with anyone, and no one mixes with you. Musa commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or go near him.

Qatada said: their remnants today say this: "No touching." It is also said that Musa intended to kill the Samiri, but God said: "Do not kill him, for he is generous." In some books it is said: if anyone from outside touches any of them, the fever seizes both of them at the same time.

﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or go near him.

﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 6/49.]]

That is, *ahassna*.

﴿We will surely burn it﴾. The common recitation has a damma on the nun and a shadda on the ra', meaning: we will burn it with fire. Al-Hasan recited it with a damma on the nun and a light ra', meaning burning with fire, and Ibn 'Abbas's statement confirms this: "He burned it with fire, then scattered it into the sea." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaysin and Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited *lanahruqanhu* with a fatha on the nun and a damma on a light ra', meaning: we will grind it with files. It is said: *haraqahu* and *yahruquhu* when he filed it down, and from this the file is called *al-muhriq*. The evidence for this reading is the statement of al-Suddi: Musa took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it into the sea. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "We will slaughter it, then we will burn it."

﴿Then we will surely scatter it﴾, that is, we will winnow it, ﴿into the sea, with a scattering.﴾ It is said: *nasafa al-ta'am bi-l-minsaf*, when one winnows the grain with a winnowing fork, scattering it and blowing away its husks and dust.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 77–97:

And We revealed to Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾, meaning: set out with them at the beginning of the night from the land of Egypt.

﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾, dry, with no water or mud in it. ﴿You will not fear being overtaken﴾ by Pharaoh behind you, ﴿nor will you fear drowning﴾ in the sea ahead of you. Hamza recited ﴿la takhaf﴾ with a jussive (*jazm*) on the basis of prohibition (*nahy*), while the rest recited it with an alif on the basis of negation (*nafy*). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading because of the following ﴿wa la takhsha﴾ in the raised form (*raf'*). The evidence for Hamza's reading is the verse ﴿They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped﴾, where the sentence is resumed (*fa-istaana'a*). Al-Farra' said: "If Hamza intended the jussive with ﴿wa la takhsha﴾, it would be correct." A poet said:

*"You satirized a time, then you turned back, making excuses,*
*for one who abused a time that neither satirized nor harmed."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/228.]]

Another said:

*"Has there not come to you, while the news spreads,*
*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/492.]]

*for one who abused a time that neither satirized nor harmed."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/228.]]

*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*

This is the answer to Pharaoh's words: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. So God contradicted him, saying: ﴿Rather, He led them astray and did not guide them.﴾

Wahb said: The Children of Israel borrowed much jewelry from the Copts, then Musa set out with them at the beginning of the night. They numbered seventy thousand. Pharaoh was informed of this, so he rode out with six hundred thousand men from the Copts, tracing the trail of Musa. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "tracing their trail."] When the people of Musa saw the dust of the horses, they said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾. Musa said: ﴿No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾. When they drew near, they said: "O Musa, where shall we go? The sea is before us and Pharaoh is behind us." Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it split, becoming twelve dry paths, one for each tribe. Between every two paths was something like a great mountain of water. They passed through it, and they were all cousins, so that each tribe could not see the others. They grew lonely and afraid. God, glorified be He, revealed to the mountains of water: "Interlace!" So they became lattices, so that some could see one another and some could hear one another's speech.

When Pharaoh reached the shore, he found that Musa and the Children of Israel had crossed. He said to the Copts: "The sea has been bewitched, so cross." They said to him: "If you are a lord, then enter the sea as it did." Jibril came on a mare in heat [in the Isfahan manuscript: "wa-dhaq"], while Pharaoh was on a stallion, the male of horses. Jibril drove the mare into the water, and Pharaoh's stallion could not restrain itself; it plunged into the sea following her trail, and all the Copts entered after him. When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

Ka'b said: The Samiri recognised the horse of Jibril, so he took a handful of dust from its track and threw it into the calf when he made it. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "when they made it."]

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Qatada said: the Samiri was a great man among the Children of Israel, from a tribe called Samira, but the enemy of God became a hypocrite after the crossing of the sea with the Children of Israel. When the Children of Israel passed by the Amalekites, who were ﴿devoted to idols of theirs﴾, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ The Samiri seized the opportunity and made the calf. Then the Samiri said in answer to Musa: ﴿I saw what they did not see﴾, meaning I saw what they had not seen, recognised what they had not recognised, and perceived what they had not perceived. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited *tabsuru* with a ta' as an address; the rest recited it with a ya' as a report. ﴿So I took a handful from the track of the Messenger﴾, that is, I took dust from the track of Jibril's horse. Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa said to him: ﴿Go, for in your life you will say, "No touching"﴾, that is, as long as you live you shall say: do not mix with anyone, and no one mixes with you. Musa commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or go near him.

Qatada said: their remnants today say this: "No touching." It is also said that Musa intended to kill the Samiri, but God said: "Do not kill him, for he is generous." In some books it is said: if anyone from outside touches any of them, the fever seizes both of them at the same time.

﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. *"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*

They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*

[In the Isfahan manuscript: "tracing their trail."] When the people of Musa saw the dust of the horses, they said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾. Musa said: ﴿No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾. When they drew near, they said: "O Musa, where shall we go? The sea is before us and Pharaoh is behind us." Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it split, becoming twelve dry paths, one for each tribe. Between every two paths was something like a great mountain of water. They passed through it, and they were all cousins, so that each tribe could not see the others. They grew lonely and afraid. God, glorified be He, revealed to the mountains of water: "Interlace!" So they became lattices, so that some could see one another and some could hear one another's speech.

When Pharaoh reached the shore, he found that Musa and the Children of Israel had crossed. He said to the Copts: "The sea has been bewitched, so cross." They said to him: "If you are a lord, then enter the sea as it did." Jibril came on a mare in heat [in the Isfahan manuscript: "wa-dhaq"], while Pharaoh was on a stallion, the male of horses. Jibril drove the mare into the water, and Pharaoh's stallion could not restrain itself; it plunged into the sea following her trail, and all the Copts entered after him. When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

Ka'b said: The Samiri recognised the horse of Jibril, so he took a handful of dust from its track and threw it into the calf when he made it. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "when they made it."]

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Eat of the good things that We have provided for you.﴾ This is the reading of the common recitation with the nun and the alif, in the plural of majesty. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Qatada said: the Samiri was a great man among the Children of Israel, from a tribe called Samira, but the enemy of God became a hypocrite after the crossing of the sea with the Children of Israel. When the Children of Israel passed by the Amalekites, who were ﴿devoted to idols of theirs﴾, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ The Samiri seized the opportunity and made the calf. Then the Samiri said in answer to Musa: ﴿I saw what they did not see﴾, meaning I saw what they had not seen, recognised what they had not recognised, and perceived what they had not perceived. Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa said to him: ﴿Go, for in your life you will say, "No touching"﴾, that is, as long as you live you shall say: do not mix with anyone, and no one mixes with you. Musa commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or go near him.

Qatada said: their remnants today say this: "No touching." It is also said that Musa intended to kill the Samiri, but God said: "Do not kill him, for he is generous." In some books it is said: if anyone from outside touches any of them, the fever seizes both of them at the same time.

﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 6/49.]]

That is, *ahassna*.

﴿We will surely burn it﴾. The common recitation has a damma on the nun and a shadda on the ra', meaning: we will burn it with fire. Al-Hasan recited it with a damma on the nun and a light ra', meaning burning with fire, and Ibn 'Abbas's statement confirms this: "He burned it with fire, then scattered it into the sea." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaysin and Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited *lanahruqanhu* with a fatha on the nun and a damma on a light ra', meaning: we will grind it with files. It is said: *haraqahu* and *yahruquhu* when he filed it down, and from this the file is called *al-muhriq*. The evidence for this reading is the statement of al-Suddi: Musa took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it into the sea. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "We will slaughter it, then we will burn it."

﴿Then we will surely scatter it﴾, that is, we will winnow it, ﴿into the sea, with a scattering.﴾ It is said: *nasafa al-ta'am bi-l-minsaf*, when one winnows the grain with a winnowing fork, scattering it and blowing away its husks and dust.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 77–97:

And We revealed to Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾, meaning: set out with them at the beginning of the night from the land of Egypt.

﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾, dry, with no water or mud in it. ﴿You will not fear being overtaken﴾ by Pharaoh behind you, ﴿nor will you fear drowning﴾ in the sea ahead of you. Hamza recited ﴿la takhaf﴾ with a jussive (*jazm*) on the basis of prohibition (*nahy*), while the rest recited it with an alif on the basis of negation (*nafy*). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading because of the following ﴿wa la takhsha﴾ in the raised form (*raf'*). The evidence for Hamza's reading is the verse ﴿They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped﴾, where the sentence is resumed (*fa-istaana'a*). Al-Farra' said: "If Hamza intended the jussive with ﴿wa la takhsha﴾, it would be correct." A poet said:

*"You satirized a time, then you turned back, making excuses,*
*for one who abused a time that neither satirized nor harmed."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/228.]]

Another said:

*"Has there not come to you, while the news spreads,*
*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/492.]]
