Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 6/49.]]

That is, *ahassna*.

﴿We will surely burn it﴾. The common recitation has a damma on the nun and a shadda on the ra', meaning: we will burn it with fire. Al-Hasan recited it with a damma on the nun and a light ra', meaning burning with fire, and Ibn 'Abbas's statement confirms this: "He burned it with fire, then scattered it into the sea." Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaysin and Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited *lanahruqanhu* with a fatha on the nun and a damma on a light ra', meaning: we will grind it with files. It is said: *haraqahu* and *yahruquhu* when he filed it down, and from this the file is called *al-muhriq*. The evidence for this reading is the statement of al-Suddi: Musa took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it into the sea. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "We will slaughter it, then we will burn it."

﴿Then we will surely scatter it﴾, that is, we will winnow it, ﴿into the sea, with a scattering.﴾ It is said: *nasafa al-ta'am bi-l-minsaf*, when one winnows the grain with a winnowing fork, scattering it and blowing away its husks and dust.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 77–97:

And We revealed to Musa: ﴿Travel by night with My servants﴾, meaning: set out with them at the beginning of the night from the land of Egypt.

﴿So strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾, dry, with no water or mud in it. ﴿You will not fear being overtaken﴾ by Pharaoh behind you, ﴿nor will you fear drowning﴾ in the sea ahead of you. Hamza recited ﴿la takhaf﴾ with a jussive (*jazm*) on the basis of prohibition (*nahy*), while the rest recited it with an alif on the basis of negation (*nafy*). Abu 'Ubayd preferred this reading because of the following ﴿wa la takhsha﴾ in the raised form (*raf'*). The evidence for Hamza's reading is the verse ﴿They will turn their backs to you, then they will not be helped﴾, where the sentence is resumed (*fa-istaana'a*). Al-Farra' said: "If Hamza intended the jussive with ﴿wa la takhsha﴾, it would be correct." A poet said:

*"You satirized a time, then you turned back, making excuses,*
*for one who abused a time that neither satirized nor harmed."*
[[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/228.]]

Another said:

*"Has there not come to you, while the news spreads,*
*what the she-camels of the Banu Ziyad suffered?"*
[[Lisan al-'Arab: 15/492.]]

﴿Then Pharaoh followed them with his armies, and the sea covered them with what covered them.﴾ That is, the waters struck them. ﴿Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.﴾ That is, he did not guide them to their right course. This is the answer to Pharaoh's words: ﴿I show you only what I see, and I guide you only to the path of right conduct﴾. So God contradicted him, saying: ﴿Rather, He led them astray and did not guide them.﴾

Wahb said: The Children of Israel borrowed much jewelry from the Copts, then Musa set out with them at the beginning of the night. They numbered seventy thousand. Pharaoh was informed of this, so he rode out with six hundred thousand men from the Copts, tracing the trail of Musa. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "tracing their trail."] When the people of Musa saw the dust of the horses, they said: ﴿Indeed we are overtaken﴾. Musa said: ﴿No! Indeed my Lord is with me; He will guide me﴾. When they drew near, they said: "O Musa, where shall we go? The sea is before us and Pharaoh is behind us." Musa struck the sea with his staff, and it split, becoming twelve dry paths, one for each tribe. Between every two paths was something like a great mountain of water. They passed through it, and they were all cousins, so that each tribe could not see the others. They grew lonely and afraid. God, glorified be He, revealed to the mountains of water: "Interlace!" So they became lattices, so that some could see one another and some could hear one another's speech.

When Pharaoh reached the shore, he found that Musa and the Children of Israel had crossed. He said to the Copts: "The sea has been bewitched, so cross." They said to him: "If you are a lord, then enter the sea as it did." Jibril came on a mare in heat [in the Isfahan manuscript: "wa-dhaq"], while Pharaoh was on a stallion, the male of horses. Jibril drove the mare into the water, and Pharaoh's stallion could not restrain itself; it plunged into the sea following her trail, and all the Copts entered after him. When they were fully in, God, glorified be He, revealed to the sea: "Drown them!" The water rose over them and drowned them.

Ka'b said: The Samiri recognised the horse of Jibril, so he took a handful of dust from its track and threw it into the calf when he made it. [In the Isfahan manuscript: "when they made it."]

﴿O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy﴾, Pharaoh, ﴿and We made an appointment with you at the right side of the mountain﴾, which has already been mentioned, ﴿and We sent down to you the manna and the quail. Eat of the good things that We have provided for you.﴾ This is the reading of the common recitation with the nun and the alif, in the plural of majesty. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿anjaytukum, wa-wa'adnakum, wa-razaqnakum﴾ without the alif, in the singular form. ﴿Eat of the lawful good things that We have provided for you.﴾

﴿And do not transgress therein.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: do not wrong. Muqatil said: do not disobey. Al-Kalbi said: do not disbelieve the blessing. It was said: do not forbid what is lawful. It was said: do not spend in disobedience to Me. It was said: do not hoard. It was said: do not use My blessings to strengthen yourselves in My disobedience.

﴿Then My anger will descend upon you﴾, meaning it will be due upon you, ﴿and whoever My anger descends upon, he has indeed fallen﴾. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash and al-Kisa'i recited ﴿fa-yahulla﴾ and ﴿man yahlul﴾ with a damma on the ha' and the lam, meaning "descends."

﴿So he has indeed fallen﴾, meaning he perished and plunged into the Fire. ﴿But indeed I am most forgiving toward one who repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then remains guided.﴾

Qatada and Sufyan al-Thawri said: it means he adheres to Islam until he dies upon it.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: he learns knowledge so that he may be guided how to act.

Al-Sha'bi, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: he knows that there is reward for that.

Fudayl al-Nakha'i and Sahl al-Tustari said: he remains upon the Sunna (the prophetic normative path) and the Community (*jama'a*).

Al-Dahhak said: it means he stays on the straight path.

﴿What hastened you away from your people?﴾ That is: what moved you to haste away from your people, namely the seventy whom Musa had chosen when they went with him to the mountain to receive the Torah from his Lord. When Musa set out in haste, out of longing for his Lord, he left the seventy behind, and he commanded them to follow him to the mountain. God, glorified be He, said to him: ﴿What hastened you from your people, O Musa?﴾ He answered his Lord: ﴿They are on my track﴾, meaning these people are coming after me. ﴿And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased﴾, that You may increase in good pleasure.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed We have tried your people﴾, tested them, ﴿those whom you left behind with Harun﴾, and they numbered six hundred thousand. They fell into temptation by the calf, except twelve thousand, ﴿after you﴾, that is, after your departure to the mountain. ﴿And the Samiri misled them﴾, meaning he called them and turned them to the worship of the calf and drove them to it.

So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved (*asif*), anxious and distressed. He said: ﴿O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?﴾, meaning a true promise, that He would give you the Torah. ﴿Has the time seemed long to you?﴾, meaning the period of my separation from you. ﴿Or did you want anger from your Lord to descend upon you, so that you broke your appointment with me?﴾ This was because God, glorified be He, had appointed thirty nights for Musa, then completed them with ten. When the thirty had passed, the enemy of God, the Samiri, said...

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: The Samiri was from the people of Kirman. He said to them: "This has only befallen you as punishment for the jewelry you have with you," and it was jewelry they had borrowed from the Copts. "So bring it and gather it until Musa comes and decides about it." It was gathered and handed to him, and he fashioned from it a calf in three days. Then he cast into it the handful he had taken from the track of Jibril's horse. The people of Musa said to him: ﴿We did not break our appointment with you by our own power﴾. The people of Medina and 'Asim recited *bi-malkina* with a fatha on the mim; Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf recited it with a damma on the mim; the rest recited it with a kasra. Their meaning is: by our authority, our capacity and our power.

Muqatil said: that is, while we ourselves hold our affairs. It was said: by our choice.

﴿But we were laden with burdens﴾. The people of the Hijaz, al-Sham and Hafs recited *hummilna* with a damma on the ha' and a shadda on the mim. The rest recited *hamalna* with a fatha on the ha' and a light mim. ﴿Burdens﴾ means loads and weights, ﴿of the ornaments of the people﴾, that is, the jewelry of Pharaoh's people. ﴿So we threw them﴾, that is, we gathered them and handed them to the Samiri, ﴿and so the Samiri cast in what he had of the jewelry﴾, just as we had cast ours. ﴿Then he brought out for them a calf, a body﴾ without life, ﴿having a lowing﴾, a sound. He had made for them a calf of gold inlaid with jewels. It lowed only once and then never again.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun came upon the Samiri while he was making the calf. He said: "What are you doing?" He said: "I am making what benefits and does not harm." Harun said: "O God, give him what he asked of You, in accordance with what is in his certainty." When he said: "O God, I ask You that it may low," it lowed, and he prostrated. It lowed only in response to Harun's supplication. ﴿So they said: This is your god and the god of Musa﴾, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he strayed and erred from the path. It was also said: the meaning is that he left it here and went out to seek him.

God, glorified be He, said: ﴿Do they not see that it does not return to them a word﴾, meaning that it does not speak to them, ﴿nor does it possess for them harm or benefit?﴾ That is, the calf does not speak to them nor answer them. It was said: it does not return to lowing and sound.

﴿Harun had already told them before: O my people, you have only been tested by it﴾, that is, you have been tried by the calf, ﴿and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me﴾ in my religion ﴿and obey my command﴾, so do not worship it. They said: ﴿We will not cease to remain devoted to it until Musa returns to us.﴾ That is, we will not stop remaining in its worship until Musa returns to us. So Harun withdrew from them with the twelve thousand who had not worshipped the calf. When Musa returned and heard the shouting and tumult, for they were dancing around the calf, the seventy who were with him said: "This is the sound of trial."

When Harun saw him, he seized his hair with his right hand and his beard with his left, and he said: ﴿O Harun, what prevented you, when you saw them going astray, that you did not follow me?﴾ They had erred and associated others with God. ﴿That you did not follow me﴾, that is, that you did not follow my command and my instruction, and it was not a matter of kinship. It was also said: the meaning is: what prevented you from joining me and informing me of their misguidance, so that your separation from them would be a rebuke and a deterrent against what they had done? It was also said: the meaning is: why did you not fight them, since you knew that if I had been among them I would have fought them against their disbelief?

﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ Harun said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. Al-Kalbi and others said: he was his brother on both his father's and mother's side, but by his words "O son of my mother" he intended to soften him and win his sympathy so that he would leave him alone. It was also said: he was his brother only on his mother's side and not his father's, and it was also said: because the mother's relation is certain while the father's is by legal presumption.

﴿Do not seize my beard or my head﴾, meaning my locks and the hair of my head, since these are two members that are protected and that are sought out for honour and reverence above all other members. ﴿Indeed I feared﴾ that if I had objected to them, they would have become two factions, some killing others, ﴿so you would say: You have caused division among the Children of Israel﴾ and brought about separation between them, ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾, and did not guard my instruction when I said to you: ﴿Take my place among my people and put things right﴾.

Qatada said concerning this verse: the righteous ones mentioned the division before you. Then Musa turned to the Samiri and said: ﴿What is your business?﴾, meaning: what is your affair and situation, and what moved you to do what you did, O Samiri? Qatada said: the Samiri was a great man among the Children of Israel, from a tribe called Samira, but the enemy of God became a hypocrite after the crossing of the sea with the Children of Israel. When the Children of Israel passed by the Amalekites, who were ﴿devoted to idols of theirs﴾, they said: ﴿O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods.﴾ The Samiri seized the opportunity and made the calf. Then the Samiri said in answer to Musa: ﴿I saw what they did not see﴾, meaning I saw what they had not seen, recognised what they had not recognised, and perceived what they had not perceived. Yahya ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, Hamza and al-Kisa'i recited *tabsuru* with a ta' as an address; the rest recited it with a ya' as a report. ﴿So I took a handful from the track of the Messenger﴾, that is, I took dust from the track of Jibril's horse. Al-Hasan recited *faqabassu qabsatan* with a sad in both places. The difference between them is that *qabd* is gathering the palm, while *qabs* is with the fingertips. ﴿So I threw it⌋, that is, I cast it into the calf. ﴿Thus my soul adorned for me﴾. Musa said to him: ﴿Go, for in your life you will say, "No touching"﴾, that is, as long as you live you shall say: do not mix with anyone, and no one mixes with you. Musa commanded the Children of Israel not to mix with him or go near him.

Qatada said: their remnants today say this: "No touching." It is also said that Musa intended to kill the Samiri, but God said: "Do not kill him, for he is generous." In some books it is said: if anyone from outside touches any of them, the fever seizes both of them at the same time.

﴿And for you, O Samiri, there is an appointment﴾ for your punishment, ﴿which you will not be able to break﴾. Al-Hasan, Qatada, Abu Nahik and Abu 'Amr recited *lan tukhlafahu* with a kasra on the lam, meaning you will not be absent from it but will meet it. The rest recited it with a fatha on the lam, meaning God will not make it fail for you.

﴿And look at your god﴾, according to your claim, and at the object of your worship, ﴿to which you remained devoted﴾, that is, which you continued to worship, remaining in it. The Arabs say: *zaltu af'alu kadha* meaning *zaltu*, *massa* meaning *massastu*, and *ahassa* meaning *ahassstu*. A poet said:

*"Except that the noble camels of the mounts*
*sensed him, so they came to him, eager."*

That is, *ahassna*.

Abu Ja'far, Ibn Muhaysin and Ashhab al-'Uqayli recited *lanahruqanhu* with a fatha on the nun and a damma on a light ra', meaning: we will grind it with files. It is said: *haraqahu* and *yahruquhu* when he filed it down, and from this the file is called *al-muhriq*. The evidence for this reading is the statement of al-Suddi: Musa took the calf, slaughtered it, then burned it with a file, then scattered it into the sea. In the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "We will slaughter it, then we will burn it."

﴿Then we will surely scatter it﴾, that is, we will winnow it, ﴿into the sea, with a scattering.﴾ It is said: *nasafa al-ta'am bi-l-minsaf*, when one winnows the grain with a winnowing fork, scattering it and blowing away its husks and dust.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 98–114:

﴿Indeed, your God is Allah, there is no god but Him.﴾ *La al-'ijl* ﴿He has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: He knows them all and His knowledge does not strain against them. It is said: "So-and-so is capable (*yasa'u*) of this matter" when he is able to bear it and is strong enough for it. ﴿Thus We relate to you some of the news of what has passed﴾ of the matters that preceded. ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾ turns his back on it, neither believing in it nor acting by what it contains, ﴿indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾, a great sin and a heavy load, ﴿abiding therein﴾, ﴿nothing will remove it.﴾

﴿And evil will it be for them on the Day of Resurrection as a burden, the Day the Horn is blown.﴾ The majority of readers recited it with a *ya'* with damma, in the passive form. Abu 'Amr recited it with a *nun* with fatha, in line with His saying ﴿And We will gather the criminals﴾, the polytheists, ﴿that Day, blue-eyed.﴾ The Arabs regarded blueness of the eyes as a bad omen. A poet satirising a man said:

Your eyes have turned blue, O son of Mak'bar,
as every Dabbi, from baseness, is blue-eyed.
(*Lisan al-'Arab*: 10/139)

It is also said that it means blind.

﴿They will whisper among themselves﴾, saying to one another, ﴿"You remained not but ten"﴾, meaning, while they were in the world, and it is said: in the graves, ﴿"but ten [nights]"﴾, meaning ten nights.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿We know best what they say when their most just in conduct says, "You remained not but a day."﴾ That is, the one most sound in intellect and soundest in judgement. ﴿You remained not but a day﴾: this shortened it in their eyes compared with the terrors of the Day of Resurrection that awaited them.

﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with blasting."﴾ That is, He will uproot them from their places and cast them into the seas until they level out.

If it is asked: what is the reason for the *fa'* in His saying ﴿Say﴾, unlike its counterparts in the Qur'an?

The answer is that those (other) questions had already been asked of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the answer came immediately after the question. This question, however, had not yet been asked, but Allah, glorified is He, knew that they would ask about it, so He answered before the question. Its sense is: "And if they ask you about the mountains, say: My Lord will blow them away with blasting, ﴿and leave it as a level plain﴾, a smooth ground with no vegetation in it, ﴿in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.﴾"

Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-'awaj* is curvature, and *al-amt* is hills and protrusions.

Mujahid said: *al-'awaj* is depression, and *al-amt* is elevation.

Ibn Zayd said: *al-amt* is unevenness and inequality. The Arabs say: "I filled the waterskin with water, with no *amt* in it," meaning, with no slackness.

Yaman said: *al-amt* is the cracks in the earth.

﴿On that Day they will follow the summoner﴾ who calls them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and he is Israfil, ﴿with no deviation from him﴾, meaning from his summons. Most scholars said: this is an inversion (*maqlub*), meaning there is no swerving for them from his summons, and they do not deviate from him; rather, they follow him swiftly.

﴿And voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you hear nothing but whispers.﴾ Voices are described as being humbled, but the meaning is "to their owners." ﴿Nothing but whispers﴾ means the sound of footsteps and their passage to the place of gathering. Its origin is a hidden sound; it is said: "So-and-so whispered his speech" when he concealed it and kept it hidden. The rajaz poet said:

And they walk with us in a gentle gait,
if the birds speak true, we shall be fortunate.

By *al-hams* is meant the sound of camels' soft feet.

Mujahid said: it is the muffled speech and the lowering of the voice.

﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves.﴾ That is, permits him to intercede and approves his word.

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them.﴾ The pronoun refers to those who follow the summoner.

﴿But they cannot encompass it in knowledge.﴾ They cannot grasp it and do not know what He will do with them.

﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer.﴾ That is, they will be abased, submit and yield. From this comes the word *'aan* for a captive. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

A King over the throne of the heavens, the Guardian,
before whose might faces are humbled and prostrate.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/248)

Talq ibn Habib said: it means prostration.

﴿And he has failed who carries injustice﴾, that is, shirk.

﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will not fear injustice or diminishment.﴾ Ibn Kathir recited it in the prohibitive form, as a response to His saying ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾, while the rest recited it as a declarative: ﴿he will not fear.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: he will not fear that evil deeds will be added to his account or that good deeds will be reduced.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliya said: no reduction will be made in the reward of his good deeds, and no sin of a wrongdoer will be laid upon him.

Al-Dahhak said: he will not be taken to account for a sin he did not commit, nor will a good deed he performed be nullified. The root of *al-hadm* is diminution and breaking. It is said: "I reduced (*hadamtu*) some of your right for you," meaning I lowered it; and "the food was digested (*hadama al-ta'am*)"; and "a woman with a *hadim* flank" means one with a flat belly.

﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they will fear Allah or it will produce for them a reminder.﴾ *Sarrafna* means "We have made clear"; *dhikran* means admonition and lesson. Qatada said: it means diligence and piety.

﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed.﴾ Ya'qub recited it with a fatha on the *nun* and on both *ya'*s. The others recited it with a damma on the first *ya'* and the last, and a sukun on the middle one.

Mujahid and Qatada said: do not recite it to your companions or dictate it to them until its meaning has become clear to you. This prohibits reciting the verse that has just descended to him and dictating it to his companions before its meaning has been explained. This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

In the other narrations it is said: when Jibril brought the revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) would recite it along with Jibril, and Jibril would not finish what he intended to recite before the Prophet (ﷺ) began its beginning, out of his eagerness for what was being revealed to him and his concern for the Qur'an, fearing that it would slip away or be forgotten. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from this, and said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, that is, with reciting the Qur'an, ﴿before its revelation to you is completed﴾, that is, before Jibril finishes reciting it to you.

﴿And say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."﴾ That is, in understanding of the Qur'an. It is also said: in memorisation. A parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ (75:16).

A King over the throne of the heavens, the Guardian,
before whose might faces are humbled and prostrate.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/248)

Talq ibn Habib said: it means prostration.

﴿And he has failed who carries injustice﴾, that is, shirk.

﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will not fear injustice or diminishment.﴾ Ibn Kathir recited it in the prohibitive form, as a response to His saying ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾, while the rest recited it as a declarative: ﴿he will not fear.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: he will not fear that evil deeds will be added to his account or that good deeds will be reduced.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliya said: no reduction will be made in the reward of his good deeds, and no sin of a wrongdoer will be laid upon him.

Al-Dahhak said: he will not be taken to account for a sin he did not commit, nor will a good deed he performed be nullified. The root of *al-hadm* is diminution and breaking. It is said: "I reduced (*hadamtu*) some of your right for you," meaning I lowered it; and "the food was digested (*hadama al-ta'am*)"; and "a woman with a *hadim* flank" means one with a flat belly.

﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they will fear Allah or it will produce for them a reminder.﴾ *Sarrafna* means "We have made clear"; *dhikran* means admonition and lesson. Qatada said: it means diligence and piety.

﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed.﴾ Ya'qub recited it with a fatha on the *nun* and on both *ya'*s. The others recited it with a damma on the first *ya'* and the last, and a sukun on the middle one.

Mujahid and Qatada said: do not recite it to your companions or dictate it to them until its meaning has become clear to you. This prohibits reciting the verse that has just descended to him and dictating it to his companions before its meaning has been explained. This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

In the other narrations it is said: when Jibril brought the revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) would recite it along with Jibril, and Jibril would not finish what he intended to recite before the Prophet (ﷺ) began its beginning, out of his eagerness for what was being revealed to him and his concern for the Qur'an, fearing that it would slip away or be forgotten. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from this, and said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, that is, with reciting the Qur'an, ﴿before its revelation to you is completed﴾, that is, before Jibril finishes reciting it to you.

﴿And say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."﴾ That is, in understanding of the Qur'an. It is also said: in memorisation. A parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ (75:16).

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 20, verses 98–114:

﴿Indeed, your God is Allah, there is no god but Him.﴾ *La al-'ijl* ﴿He has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾: He knows them all and His knowledge does not strain against them. It is said: "So-and-so is capable (*yasa'u*) of this matter" when he is able to bear it and is strong enough for it. ﴿Thus We relate to you some of the news of what has passed﴾ of the matters that preceded. ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an. ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾ turns his back on it, neither believing in it nor acting by what it contains, ﴿indeed, he will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾, a great sin and a heavy load, ﴿abiding therein﴾, ﴿nothing will remove it.﴾

﴿And evil will it be for them on the Day of Resurrection as a burden, the Day the Horn is blown.﴾ The majority of readers recited it with a *ya'* with damma, in the passive form. Abu 'Amr recited it with a *nun* with fatha, in line with His saying ﴿And We will gather the criminals﴾, the polytheists, ﴿that Day, blue-eyed.﴾ The Arabs regarded blueness of the eyes as a bad omen. A poet satirising a man said:

Your eyes have turned blue, O son of Mak'bar,
as every Dabbi, from baseness, is blue-eyed.
(*Lisan al-'Arab*: 10/139)

It is also said that it means blind.

﴿They will whisper among themselves﴾, saying to one another, ﴿"You remained not but ten"﴾, meaning, while they were in the world, and it is said: in the graves, ﴿"but ten [nights]"﴾, meaning ten nights.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿We know best what they say when their most just in conduct says, "You remained not but a day."﴾ That is, the one most sound in intellect and soundest in judgement. ﴿You remained not but a day﴾: this shortened it in their eyes compared with the terrors of the Day of Resurrection that awaited them.

﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with blasting."﴾ That is, He will uproot them from their places and cast them into the seas until they level out.

If it is asked: what is the reason for the *fa'* in His saying ﴿Say﴾, unlike its counterparts in the Qur'an?

The answer is that those (other) questions had already been asked of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the answer came immediately after the question. This question, however, had not yet been asked, but Allah, glorified is He, knew that they would ask about it, so He answered before the question. Its sense is: "And if they ask you about the mountains, say: My Lord will blow them away with blasting, ﴿and leave it as a level plain﴾, a smooth ground with no vegetation in it, ﴿in which you will see no crookedness or elevation.﴾"

Ibn 'Abbas said: *al-'awaj* is curvature, and *al-amt* is hills and protrusions.

Mujahid said: *al-'awaj* is depression, and *al-amt* is elevation.

Ibn Zayd said: *al-amt* is unevenness and inequality. The Arabs say: "I filled the waterskin with water, with no *amt* in it," meaning, with no slackness.

Yaman said: *al-amt* is the cracks in the earth.

﴿On that Day they will follow the summoner﴾ who calls them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and he is Israfil, ﴿with no deviation from him﴾, meaning from his summons. Most scholars said: this is an inversion (*maqlub*), meaning there is no swerving for them from his summons, and they do not deviate from him; rather, they follow him swiftly.

﴿And voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you hear nothing but whispers.﴾ Voices are described as being humbled, but the meaning is "to their owners." ﴿Nothing but whispers﴾ means the sound of footsteps and their passage to the place of gathering. Its origin is a hidden sound; it is said: "So-and-so whispered his speech" when he concealed it and kept it hidden. The rajaz poet said:

And they walk with us in a gentle gait,
if the birds speak true, we shall be fortunate.

By *al-hams* is meant the sound of camels' soft feet.

Mujahid said: it is the muffled speech and the lowering of the voice.

﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful permits and whose word He approves.﴾ That is, permits him to intercede and approves his word.

﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them.﴾ The pronoun refers to those who follow the summoner.

﴿But they cannot encompass it in knowledge.﴾ They cannot grasp it and do not know what He will do with them.

﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer.﴾ That is, they will be abased, submit and yield. From this comes the word *'aan* for a captive. Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

A King over the throne of the heavens, the Guardian,
before whose might faces are humbled and prostrate.
(Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 11/248)

Talq ibn Habib said: it means prostration.

﴿And he has failed who carries injustice﴾, that is, shirk.

﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will not fear injustice or diminishment.﴾ Ibn Kathir recited it in the prohibitive form, as a response to His saying ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾, while the rest recited it as a declarative: ﴿he will not fear.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: he will not fear that evil deeds will be added to his account or that good deeds will be reduced.

Al-Hasan and Abu al-'Aliya said: no reduction will be made in the reward of his good deeds, and no sin of a wrongdoer will be laid upon him.

Al-Dahhak said: he will not be taken to account for a sin he did not commit, nor will a good deed he performed be nullified. The root of *al-hadm* is diminution and breaking. It is said: "I reduced (*hadamtu*) some of your right for you," meaning I lowered it; and "the food was digested (*hadama al-ta'am*)"; and "a woman with a *hadim* flank" means one with a flat belly.

﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they will fear Allah or it will produce for them a reminder.﴾ *Sarrafna* means "We have made clear"; *dhikran* means admonition and lesson. Qatada said: it means diligence and piety.

﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed.﴾ Ya'qub recited it with a fatha on the *nun* and on both *ya'*s. The others recited it with a damma on the first *ya'* and the last, and a sukun on the middle one.

Mujahid and Qatada said: do not recite it to your companions or dictate it to them until its meaning has become clear to you. This prohibits reciting the verse that has just descended to him and dictating it to his companions before its meaning has been explained. This is the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas.

In the other narrations it is said: when Jibril brought the revelation, the Prophet (ﷺ) would recite it along with Jibril, and Jibril would not finish what he intended to recite before the Prophet (ﷺ) began its beginning, out of his eagerness for what was being revealed to him and his concern for the Qur'an, fearing that it would slip away or be forgotten. So Allah, glorified is He, forbade him from this, and said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an﴾, that is, with reciting the Qur'an, ﴿before its revelation to you is completed﴾, that is, before Jibril finishes reciting it to you.

﴿And say, "My Lord, increase me in knowledge."﴾ That is, in understanding of the Qur'an. It is also said: in memorisation. A parallel is His saying: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it﴾ (75:16).

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that.
