It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. He said "ends" (aṭrāf) for these two prayers because the noon prayer is at the end of the first portion of the day, and at the beginning of the other portion of the day, so it is at two ends of it, and the third end is the sunset, and at that time one prays the sunset prayer. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".

﴿So that you may be well-pleased﴾, with intercession and reward. The majority of readers read it with a fatha on the tāʾ (tarḍā). Its evidence is His words: ﴿And your Lord will surely give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Ḍuḥā 93:5]. al-Kisai and ʿAsim, in the narration of Abu Bakr, read it with a ḍamma on the tāʾ (turḍā).

﴿And do not extend your eyes...﴾ (the verse).

Abu Rafiʿ said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, but he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, so Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, meaning do not look at ﴿what We have given to some pairs of them﴾, meaning We have given them categories of worldly bliss, ﴿the splendour of the life of this world﴾, meaning its adornment and radiance.

It was read by the majority with the jazm (sukun) on the hāʾ (minhum/zahratal-hayat...), and Yaʿqub read it with a fatha on it, and both are dialects, like jahrah and jahrah. He put it in the accusative as a separate construction (qaṭʿ), departing from the hāʾ in His words: "matt̲aʿnā bihi" (We have given them to enjoy).

﴿And the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin your family to prayer and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you. And the good outcome is for piety (al-taqwā)﴾, meaning for the people of piety.

Hisham ibn ʿUrwah said: When ʿUrwah saw what was with the rulers, he would enter his house and say: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾, up to His words: ﴿and the outcome is for piety﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may Allah have mercy on you."

Malik ibn Dinar said: When Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani's family suffered need, he would say: "Get up and pray," then say: "With this Allah commanded His Messenger," and recite this verse.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning these polytheists: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾, meaning Muhammad, as the prophets before him brought signs.

Allah, glorified is He, said: ﴿Has there not come to them a clear proof (bayyinah)...﴾ Read with the tāʾ (taʾtihim) by the people of Madinah, the people of Basrah and some Kufan readers, because bayyinah is feminine. The others read it with the yāʾ (yaʾtihim) because the verb was placed before the subject, and because bayyinah is explanation, so it was returned to the meaning. ﴿The clear proof of what is in the former scriptures﴾, meaning the clear explanation of what is in them, namely the Qur'an, is stronger proof and a clearer sign.

Some of the people of meanings (ahl al-maʿānī) said: It means: Has there not come to them the explanation of what is in the earlier scriptures, the Torah, the Gospel and others, and the reports of the nations that We destroyed when they asked for signs? When the signs came to them and they disbelieved in them, how We hastened punishment and destruction upon them for their disbelief. So what assures them, if a sign comes to them, that their situation would not be like those?

﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it﴾, meaning before the revelation of the Qur'an and the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ),

﴿they would have said: Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger, so that we might follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾, by punishment.

﴿Say: Each is waiting (mutarabbiṣ), so wait; you will soon know﴾, when the command of Allah, the Exalted, comes and the Resurrection is established, ﴿who are the companions of the upright path, and who has been guided﴾ from error. ﴿Is it we or you?﴾

﴿And We had certainly made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot...﴾ Allah, glorified is He, says: If these people, to whom We have set forth the threat in the Qur'an, break My covenant, oppose My command and abandon My obedience, then their father Adam (peace be upon him) did exactly that, when We made a covenant with him, meaning We commanded him and charged him, ﴿but he forgot﴾, meaning he abandoned the command and the covenant. Its parallel is His words ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them﴾ [al-Tawbah 9:67], meaning they abandoned the command of Allah, so Allah abandoned them to the Fire. This is the view of most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Ibn Zayd said: He forgot what Allah had covenanted with him concerning that. Had he had resolve, he would not have obeyed his enemy Iblis, who envied him and refused to prostrate to him, and disobeyed Allah, who honoured and ennobled him. According to this view, it is possible that Adam is taken to task for that statement by the word "forgetting", though he is, today, raised above us.

﴿And We found in him no resolve (ʿazm)﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Preservation of what he was commanded. Qatadah and Muqatil said: Patience. Ibn Zayd: Safeguarding the command of Allah and holding fast to it. al-Dahhak: Firm decision of command. ʿAtiyyah: Opinion. It is also said: Certainty. Ibn Kaysan: Persistence and inner intent to return to sin a second time. The root of ʿazm is intention and the heart's firm resolve upon a matter.

Abu Umamah said: If the forbearance (ahlam) of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, glorified is He, created Adam until the Hour rises, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh theirs. And Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And We found in him no resolve﴾.

﴿And when We said to the angels: Prostrate to Adam, they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, meaning he refused to prostrate to him. ﴿So We said: O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not expel you both from the Garden, [so that you become wretched]﴾, meaning you would become weary, and your living would be by the toil of your hand, by the sweat of your brow.

Saʿid ibn Jubayr said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. That is his "wretchedness" which Allah, glorified is He, mentioned. It should have been said: "so that you both become wretched" (fa-yashqaa), but the masculine was given precedence, referring it back to Adam, since his toil was greater. It is also said: this was for the sake of the rhyme-endings of the verses (ruʾus al-ayy).

﴿Indeed, it is for you that you will not hunger therein﴾, meaning in the Garden, ﴿nor go naked﴾. ﴿And indeed you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun﴾. Nafiʿ read wa-annaka with a kasra on the alif, as a resumption (istiʾnaf, beginning a new sentence). Abu Bakr narrated the same from ʿAsim. The rest read it with a fatha, as coordination (ʿatf, conjunction) with His words ﴿that you will not hunger﴾, meaning you will not be made to thirst by thirst therein, ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning be brought out to the sun so that its heat harms you. ʿUmar ibn Abi Rabiʿah said:

She saw a man, when the sun confronts him at noon, he is exposed to it, and in the evening he is confined.

Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbdus al-Muzakki informed us, he said: Abu al-Hasan al-Mahfuzi informed us, he said: ʿAbdullah ibn Hashim informed us, he said: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi informed us, from Sufyan, from Khusayf, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿nor be exposed to the sun﴾, meaning the sun does not touch you.

﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying: O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity (shajarat al-khuld) and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ That is, to a tree whose eating would make you remain forever, immortal, ﴿and a kingdom that does not decay﴾, meaning does not perish nor vanish.

﴿So they both ate﴾, meaning Adam and Eve, ﴿from it﴾, meaning from the tree of trial, ﴿and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to cover themselves with leaves of the Garden﴾. ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, so he went astray﴾, meaning he transgressed into what was not his to do.

Most of the exegetes said: ﴿he went astray﴾ means he erred and was misguided, and did not attain his aim from what he ate.

﴿Then his Lord chose him﴾, meaning selected him and chose him, ﴿and accepted his repentance and guided him﴾, meaning guided him to repentance and granted him success therein.

﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others﴾ [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: The enmity of the serpent means its biting, and our enmity with it is killing. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: Kill the serpent and break the covenant of Iblis. The enmity of Iblis toward us and our enmity toward him is through disbelief. So enmity is specified for Adam, Eve and Iblis, then He equated them in meaning and made them share in the enmity.

It is related in a report that Iblis said: Your servants love You and disobey You, and they hate me and obey me. Allah, the Exalted, said: I am pleased with them for their love of Me, and I forgive them for their hatred of you.]] ﴿Then, when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance﴾, meaning the Book and the Messenger, ﴿will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

Abu ʿAmr Ahmad ibn Hamdun informed us, by my reading to him, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq informed us, he said: Saʿid ibn ʿIsa [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Ishaq]] informed us, he said: Faris ibn ʿUmar informed us, and Salih ibn Muhammad informed us, he said: Yahya ibn al-Dariys informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Shaʿbi, from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾. He said: Allah protects the follower of the Qur'an from going astray in this world and from being wretched in the Hereafter.

Muhammad ibn al-Qasim informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah informed us.

Ibn al-Muqri informed me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sinan informed us, he said: al-Hasan ibn Sufyan informed us, he said: Ibn Shaybah informed us, he said: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Qays, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Allah guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an that he will not go astray in this world nor be wretched in the Hereafter, then he recited: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

And with his isnad from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, who said: Ibn Fudayl informed us, from ʿAtaʾ ibn al-Sa'ib, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, Allah guides him from error and protects him on the Day of Resurrection from a bad reckoning. That is because Allah says: ﴿Whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be wretched﴾.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning from the Qur'an, so that he does not believe in it nor follow it, ﴿indeed he will have a constricted life (maʿishatan ḍankan)﴾, narrow. It is said: a dank dwelling and a dank life, in which the masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural are alike. ʿAntarah said:

And when they alight in narrowness, you alight [...]

[[Its opening line: "So help them and rejoice in what they rejoice in." See Tafsir al-Tabari 3/341 and Lisan al-Arab 1/712 and 4/62.]]

The exegetes differed concerning "the constricted life". Abu ʿUthman Saʿid ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad al-Hiri [[In the Isfahan manuscript: Saʿid ibn Muhammad al-Hibri]] informed me, he said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Mufid informed us, he said: Abu Khalifah al-Fadl ibn al-Habbab informed us, he said: Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi informed us, he said: Hammad ibn Salamah informed us, from ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said, concerning His words: ﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a constricted life﴾: "The punishment of the grave."

Ibn ʿAbbas said: It is hardship. Mujahid: Narrowness. al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd: Zaqqum, ghislin and dari (thorny plant). Qatadah: That is in the Fire. ʿIkrimah: The unlawful. Qays ibn Abi Hazim: Provision obtained through disobedience. al-Dahhak: Wicked earning. ʿAtiyyah from Ibn ʿAbbas says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood. Indeed, a people who were astray turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and plenty in worldly matters, yet their livelihood was constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not replace their livelihood, due to their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and thinks evil of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Abu Saʿid al-Khudri: His grave is made narrow for him until his ribs interlace, and there are set upon him in his grave ninety-nine dragons (tinnin), each dragon with seven heads, biting him and tearing his flesh until he is resurrected. And if one of them were to breathe into the earth, nothing would grow there.

Muqatil: A bad livelihood, because it is in disobedience to Allah. Saʿid ibn Jubayr: He is deprived of contentment so that he is never satisfied.

﴿And We shall gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: Blind of sight. Mujahid: Blind to the proof.

﴿He will say: My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, when I was seeing?﴾ meaning with my eyes. Mujahid said: knowing my proof.

﴿He will say: Thus﴾, meaning as: ﴿Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾, meaning you abandoned them and turned away from them. ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾, meaning you are left in the Fire. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning as We recompensed the one who turned away [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: from the Qur'an]], ﴿so do We recompense him who transgresses﴾, meaning associates partners with Allah, ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is severer and more lasting﴾, meaning more lasting and enduring, than what He punishes them with in this world and in the grave.

﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk?﴾ meaning their dwellings and homes when they travel and trade.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for people of understanding (ūlī al-nuhā)﴾.

﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, the structure of the verse being: "had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord", concerning the delay of the punishment from them, ﴿and a term decreed﴾, which is the Resurrection, ﴿it would have been inevitable (lizāman)﴾, meaning the punishment would have been binding upon them in this world, as it was binding upon the disbelieving generations before them.

﴿So be patient over what they say﴾. It was abrogated (naskh, replacement of a ruling by a later one) by the verse of fighting. ﴿And glorify your Lord with the praise of your Lord﴾, meaning pray with the command of your Lord. It is also said: with the praise of your Lord, ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the dawn prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the afternoon prayer, ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, meaning the night prayer, the late evening prayer, ﴿so glorify Him, and at the ends of the day﴾, meaning the noon and sunset prayers. Therefore He said: "aṭrāf" [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "al-nahār" (the day)]]. And [[In the Isfahan manuscript there is an addition: "aṭrāf"]] is in the accusative as a coordination (ʿaṭf) with His words: "before the rising of the sun".
